anji-bai-cha.description: 'Anji White Tea'. A unique and fascinating cultivar that, despite its name, is processed as a green tea. In the low temperatures of early spring, its leaves have an albino-like appearance due to a lack of chlorophyll. This results in an exceptionally high concentration of amino acids, producing a tea with a powerful, savory 'umami' flavor unlike any other green tea.
anji-bai-cha.plantType: Delicate, temperature-sensitive bush (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
anji-bai-cha.environment: Requires a specific microclimate with a cool spring to trigger its albino phase. It thrives in the bamboo-rich terroir of Anji County.
anji-bai-cha.processing: Processing must be extremely gentle to protect the delicate, amino-acid-rich leaves. The goal is to do as little as possible to let the unique character of the raw material shine through.
anji-bai-cha.oxidation: Zero oxidation. The leaves are lightly steamed or pan-fired at a low temperature to halt oxidation while preserving their delicate structure and chemical composition.
anji-bai-cha.roasting: No roasting. The tea is simply dried at a low temperature after the kill-green step. Any roasting would destroy its unique, savory flavor.
anji-bai-cha.versatility: Extremely specialized. This cultivar is cultivated for one purpose only: to create the unique, umami-rich green tea known as Anji Bai Cha.

china: Sichuan Province (where it is also cultivated)

Green Tea.Anji Bai Cha: Its sole expression is a minimally processed green tea, designed to preserve its high amino acid content and unique umami flavor. The leaves are typically long and needle-like.

sensory.aroma: Steamed Asparagus, nuts, a subtle sweet floral note
sensory.flavor: Powerful, savory Umami, reminiscent of chicken broth, with a very sweet and clean finish.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Light-bodied but intensely flavorful and savory, with a smooth, vibrant texture. The liquor is a very pale, almost clear jade color.

asahi.description: 'Morning Sun'. An old and revered elite cultivar from Uji, Kyoto. It is considered one of the absolute highest-grade cultivars for Matcha production, prized for its supremely elegant, profoundly sweet, and umami-rich profile with almost no bitterness. It is often used for top-tier, ceremonial-grade Matcha.
asahi.plantType: Delicate, slow-growing, semi-upright bush with thin leaves (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
asahi.environment: Requires the specific, stable, and rich terroir of Uji. It is a demanding cultivar with a low yield, reserved for the best plots.
asahi.processing: Asahi is a shading master. It must be shaded for an extended period (20+ days) to develop its unique chemical composition, which is high in L-theanine and low in catechins. The leaves are very delicate and must be handled with extreme care.
asahi.oxidation: Zero oxidation. The leaves are lightly steamed immediately after harvest to preserve their delicate character.
asahi.roasting: No roasting. The leaves are processed into Tencha by being dried flat in a specialized 'tencha-ro' oven, which prepares them for stone-grinding without altering their pure flavor.
asahi.versatility: Extremely specialized. Asahi is a 'thoroughbred' cultivar used exclusively for producing the most premium, ceremonial-grade Matcha in Japan.

Matcha & Tencha.Ultra-Premium Ceremonial Matcha: Its sole and highest expression. When shaded, it produces Tencha that is stone-ground into the finest Matcha, known for its incredible sweetness and elegance.

sensory.aroma: Subtle, sweet, clean, and milky
sensory.flavor: Profound and elegant umami with an exceptional, lasting sweetness and virtually zero bitterness.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Incredibly smooth, creamy, and refined, creating a very luxurious bowl of Matcha. The liquor is a bright, vibrant green.

asatsuyu.description: 'Morning Dew'. A legendary cultivar often referred to as a 'natural Gyokuro' due to its intense, sweet umami flavor, even when grown unshaded as Sencha. It is one of the parents of the elite Saemidori cultivar and is prized by connoisseurs for its powerful, savory, and sweet character, though it can be difficult to cultivate.

ba-xian.description: 'Eight Immortals'. A powerful and assertive clonal Dan Cong cultivar, developed from eight cuttings of a venerable Song Zhong mother tree. It is renowned for its intense, almost aggressive fragrance and a strong, impactful flavor profile that sets it apart from more delicate floral types.
ba-xian.plantType: Vigorous arbor type with dark green, shiny leaves (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
ba-xian.environment: Grows in the high-altitude, rocky terroir of the Phoenix Mountains, which provides the mineral foundation for its strong character.
ba-xian.roasting: resonant finish without overpowering the core aroma.,Highly specialized. Ba Xian is a singular expression of a powerful
ba-xian.versatility:
high-aroma Dan Cong oolong and is not used for other tea styles.
Long Jing #43,龙井43号,The most widespread and commercially important modern cultivar for West Lake Long Jing tea. Developed in the 1970s

Dan Cong Oolong.Ba Xian Dan Cong: A traditionally processed Dan Cong oolong where the processing is designed to highlight its powerful fragrance and 'cha qi' (tea energy).

bai-ji-guan.description: 'White Cockscomb'. A rare and unique member of the 'Si Da Ming Cong', Bai Ji Guan stands apart from all other Wuyi oolongs. It is named for its peculiar pale, yellowish-green leaves and is processed with a much lighter hand, resulting in a creamy, sweet, and custardy flavor profile that contrasts sharply with the dark, roasty character of its famous brethren.
bai-ji-guan.plantType: Small, slow-growing, semi-upright bush with delicate branches (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
bai-ji-guan.environment: Requires a specific microclimate within the Wuyi Mountains. It is less hardy than other Yancha cultivars and requires great care.
bai-ji-guan.processing: Processing Bai Ji Guan requires immense skill and a light touch. The leaves are more fragile than other Wuyi cultivars, so the bruising and oxidation steps must be gentle to avoid bitterness and preserve its delicate aromatics.
bai-ji-guan.oxidation: Oxidation is kept very light for a Yancha (20-30%). This preserves the leaf's natural pale color and its sweet, creamy, and corn-like flavor notes.
bai-ji-guan.roasting: Roasting is minimal and done at a very low temperature. It is more of a final drying bake than a flavor-altering roast. The goal is to stabilize the tea while allowing its inherent sweetness and unique flavor to shine.
bai-ji-guan.versatility: Extremely specialized. Bai Ji Guan represents a unique, almost historical style of light Yancha. It is not versatile and can only be made in this specific way.

china: Fujian Province (Wuyi Mountains - very small production area)

Wuyi Rock Oolong (Yancha - Light Style).Bai Ji Guan Yancha: Its only expression is a lightly oxidized and lightly roasted oolong, a style designed to preserve its delicate, sweet, and creamy nature.

sensory.aroma: Delicate floral notes, sweet corn, cream, buttery pastry
sensory.flavor: Custardy, sweet, with notes of yellow summer fruits (like pawpaw or melon) and a subtle mineral finish.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Creamy, smooth, and surprisingly thick with very low astringency. The liquor is a pale, bright golden-yellow.

bai-wen.description: 'White Hairs'. A modern cultivar developed by TRES specifically for the production of leafhopper-bitten teas like Oriental Beauty. It was designed to be a more productive and pest-resistant alternative to the traditional Qing Xin Da Mao cultivar, while still being able to produce the signature honey-fruit fragrance when bitten by the tea leafhopper.
bai-wen.plantType: Vigorous, upright bush with large, downy leaves.
bai-wen.environment: Grows well in the same hot, humid, and leafhopper-rich environments as Qing Xin Da Mao in northwestern Taiwan.
bai-wen.processing: Processing is identical to that of traditional Oriental Beauty. The key is that the leaves must be bitten by the tea leafhopper to initiate the chemical changes that create the unique aroma.
bai-wen.oxidation: Undergoes heavy oxidation (60-70%) to fully develop the complex honey and fruit flavors that result from the insect bites.
bai-wen.roasting: Completely unroasted. All the flavor and aroma are developed through the natural reaction to the insect bites and the subsequent heavy oxidation.
bai-wen.versatility: Extremely specialized. This cultivar was bred for the single purpose of making Oriental Beauty oolong, offering farmers a more reliable option.

Oriental Beauty Oolong (Dong Fang Mei Re.Bai Hao Oolong: Its sole purpose is to be an alternative cultivar for making high-quality Oriental Beauty oolong.

sensory.aroma: Honey, Ripe Peach, Floral, similar to Oriental Beauty
sensory.flavor: Sweet, fruity, and complex with a smooth finish.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Full-bodied and smooth. The liquor is a bright reddish-orange.

ban-tian-yao.description: 'Half-way to the Sky'. A classic Wuyi Rock Oolong named for the legend of its original bush growing halfway up a cliff. It is celebrated for its perfect balance and elegance, often described as the ideal middle-ground Yancha—lacking the sharp spice of Rou Gui or the deep woodiness of Shui Xian, it instead offers a clear, sweet, and floral profile.
ban-tian-yao.plantType: Upright, medium-sized arbor type, well-adapted to rocky growth (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
ban-tian-yao.environment: Best expresses itself in the core 'Zhengyan' region of the Wuyi Mountains, where the mineral-rich terroir contributes to its balanced flavor.
ban-tian-yao.processing: The processing of Ban Tian Yao is a balancing act itself. The goal is not to impart extreme flavors but to reveal the cultivar's natural elegance. Its leaves are robust enough for traditional Yancha processing but shine when not pushed to extremes.
ban-tian-yao.oxidation: Undergoes a standard medium-to-heavy oxidation for Yancha (40-60%) to develop a solid foundation of flavor that enhances its floral and fruity notes.
ban-tian-yao.roasting: Typically receives a medium charcoal roast. This is enough to create the desired 'rock rhyme' and smoothness but light enough to preserve its delicate floral top notes, which could be lost with a heavier bake.
ban-tian-yao.versatility: Highly specialized. Ban Tian Yao is a pure expression of the traditional Wuyi Rock Oolong style and is not used for other types of tea.

Wuyi Rock Oolong (Yancha).Ban Tian Yao Yancha: Its sole expression is a traditionally crafted rock oolong, where processing aims to highlight its inherent balance and elegant floral character.

sensory.aroma: Delicate Orchid, Stone Fruit, Toasted Grain, faint sweetness
sensory.flavor: Clean, sweet, with a very clear and pure mineral note. Well-balanced without any single dominant flavor.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Smooth, medium-bodied, and elegant with a pleasant, lingering sweet finish. The liquor is a clear, bright amber.

bei-dou.description: 'North Star'. A prestigious Wuyi Rock Oolong cultivar directly descended from the legendary Da Hong Pao lineage. It is renowned for its powerful and robust character, thick body, and a classic roasted flavor profile that is both complex and deeply satisfying, making it a favorite among seasoned Yancha drinkers.
bei-dou.plantType: Sturdy, upright arbor type well-adapted to rocky terrain (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
bei-dou.environment: Grows best in the core 'Zhengyan' region of the Wuyi Mountains, where the mineral-rich soil and terroir create its powerful flavor.
bei-dou.processing: The processing of Bei Dou is a classic example of traditional Yancha craftsmanship. Its strong leaves can withstand the necessary heavy oxidation and multiple roasts that build its complex character.
bei-dou.oxidation: Undergoes heavy oxidation (50-60%) to develop a rich, fruity, and robust flavor base that serves as the perfect foundation for the charcoal roasting process.
bei-dou.roasting: Receives a medium-to-heavy charcoal roast, often in multiple stages. This is essential for creating its signature roasted depth, smoothing its texture, and developing the long, sweet finish.
bei-dou.versatility: Highly specialized. Bei Dou is a pure expression of the traditional, powerful Wuyi Rock Oolong style and is not used for other types of tea.

Wuyi Rock Oolong (Yancha).Bei Dou Yancha: A powerful, complex rock oolong with deep roast notes, a pronounced mineral character, and a long, sweet aftertaste.

sensory.aroma: Roasted nuts, dark chocolate, subtle florals, warm minerals
sensory.flavor: Rich, robust, and deeply mineralic with a satisfying, lingering sweetness.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Thick, viscous, and warming with a strong and comforting presence. The liquor is a deep, clear amber.

ben-shan.description: 'Original Mountain'. A close genetic relative of Tie Guan Yin from the neighboring mountains of Anxi. Ben Shan is known for producing a lighter-bodied oolong with a very clear, high-pitched floral aroma, often described as being more straightforward and less complex than its famous cousin. It is a popular and more affordable daily-drinker oolong.
ben-shan.plantType: Upright bush type, similar in appearance to Tie Guan Yin but slightly less robust (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
ben-shan.environment: Grows in similar conditions to Tie Guan Yin but is often found in slightly different microclimates within the greater Anxi region.
ben-shan.processing: Ben Shan's leaves are thinner and more delicate than Tie Guan Yin's, making them best suited for light-handed processing. They develop their floral aroma quickly but cannot withstand heavy oxidation or roasting.
ben-shan.oxidation: Oxidation is kept very low (10-20%) to preserve its fresh, delicate, and high-pitched floral notes. The goal is to maximize the upfront aroma.
ben-shan.roasting: Almost never roasted, other than a final, low-temperature drying bake. Its delicate character would be completely overwhelmed by any significant roasting.
ben-shan.versatility: Not very versatile. It excels at one thing: being a light, fresh, and aromatic green-style oolong. It lacks the substance for traditional processing or for making other tea types.

china: Fujian Province (Anxi, specifically the Daping and Changkeng areas)

Oolong Tea (Classic Expression).Anxi Oolong (Light Style): Almost exclusively made in the modern 'green' style to showcase its bright, fresh floral aroma. It is rarely roasted.

sensory.aroma: Fresh, clean floral notes (less complex than TGY), cut grass, hint of gardenia
sensory.flavor: Crisp, light, sweet, and slightly vegetal. Lacks the deep creaminess of TGY.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Lighter-bodied and thinner than Tie Guan Yin, with a clean and brisk texture. The liquor is a very pale, clear yellow-green.

benifuki.description: 'Red Riches'. Japan's most famous and important black tea cultivar. It is a powerful hybrid of Assamica varieties, bred to produce a robust, full-bodied black tea with a strong astringency and notes of plum and citrus. It is also famous for its high content of methylated catechins, which are studied for their anti-allergic properties.

benihikari.description: 'Red Light'. A classic Japanese black tea cultivar with Darjeeling lineage, known for its muscatel-like aroma.

bi-luo-chun-qunti.description: 'Bi Luo Chun Population'. The original, small-leaf heirloom population from the Dongting mountains, famous for producing one of China's top ten green teas. The bushes are traditionally interplanted with fruit trees (like apricot, plum, and loquat), and the tea is said to absorb their fragrance. The finished tea consists of tiny, downy buds that are hand-rolled into a distinctive spiral shape.
bi-luo-chun-qunti.plantType: Small, sprawling bushes with a less upright habit (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
bi-luo-chun-qunti.environment: Grows in the unique microclimate of the Dongting peninsula on Lake Tai, where the lake effect moderates temperatures and the soil is ideal. Intercropping with fruit trees is key to the traditional terroir.
bi-luo-chun-qunti.processing: The processing is incredibly laborious. The tiny, tender buds are pan-fired in a wok and simultaneously hand-rolled into their characteristic tight spiral shape. This requires immense skill to do without crushing the delicate buds.
bi-luo-chun-qunti.oxidation: Zero oxidation. The tea is pan-fired immediately after being picked to preserve its fresh, vibrant character.
bi-luo-chun-qunti.roasting: No roasting. The pan-firing process serves to both kill-green and dry the tea.
bi-luo-chun-qunti.versatility: Completely specialized. This heirloom cultivar is inextricably linked to the unique hand-processing and terroir of Dongting Bi Luo Chun.

china: Jiangsu Province (Suzhou - Dongting East and West mountains)

Green Tea.Dongting Bi Luo Chun: A very early spring green tea made from tiny, tender, and extremely downy buds. It is pan-fired and hand-rolled into tight spirals.

sensory.aroma: Intensely fruity and floral, savory, with a distinct 'xia sha xiang' (frighteningly intense aroma)
sensory.flavor: Strong umami, sweet, with complex fruity and vegetal notes and a long, refreshing finish.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Thick, brothy, and very smooth. The abundant white down on the buds creates a rich, soupy texture. The liquor is a bright yellow-green.

chin-hsin.description: 'Soothing Heart'. One of the newest cultivars released by TRES (2016), it was bred for broad appeal, combining the creamy texture of Jin Xuan with the elegant floral notes of Qing Xin. It is a modern, well-rounded cultivar designed for producing high-quality light oolongs.
chin-hsin.plantType: Upright, vigorous bush with good yield.
chin-hsin.environment: Adaptable to the mid-altitude oolong-producing regions of Taiwan.
chin-hsin.processing: Processing aims to capture the best of both its parents, requiring careful withering to develop both the creamy and floral notes simultaneously.
chin-hsin.oxidation: Undergoes light oxidation (15-30%) to maintain a fresh, aromatic profile.
chin-hsin.roasting: Unroasted, to preserve the delicate balance of its creamy and floral characteristics.
chin-hsin.versatility: Specialized for light oolongs. It was bred to be a high-quality, modern oolong and is not intended for other styles.

Oolong Tea (Light Style).Modern Light Oolong: Designed to be made into a lightly oxidized, unroasted, ball-rolled oolong that is both creamy and floral.

sensory.aroma: Creamy, Floral, Buttery
sensory.flavor: A good balance of Jin Xuan's creaminess and Qing Xin's floral elegance.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Smooth, full, and creamy. The liquor is a bright, pale gold.

cui-yu.description: 'Jade'. Developed in 1981 by Taiwan's Tea Research and Extension Station (TRES), Cui Yu was bred for its powerful, unforgettable floral aroma. Often compared to magnolia and lily, it has become a cornerstone of modern Taiwanese oolongs, beloved for its high yield and fragrant character.
cui-yu.plantType: Early-sprouting, high-yielding arbor type (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis)
cui-yu.environment: Thrives in the misty, humid conditions of mid-to-high elevations (400-1,200m). Known for its vigor and good resistance to drought.
cui-yu.processing: Cui Yu's signature floral aroma is best expressed through controlled, light processing that emphasizes its natural aromatics over heavy-roast flavors.
cui-yu.oxidation: Typically undergoes light oxidation (15-30%) for oolongs. The extended withering process is crucial for developing its complex magnolia and gardenia notes.
cui-yu.roasting: Generally unroasted or receives a very light, low-temperature finishing roast for drying purposes. Heavy roasting can easily overwhelm its delicate floral bouquet.
cui-yu.versatility: It is a versatile cultivar. While ideal for light oolongs, careful full oxidation can produce a uniquely aromatic black tea that retains some of its floral heritage.

Oolong Tea (Classic Expression).Baozhong: Lightly oxidized, twisted-leaf style that maximizes its fresh floral bouquet.
Oolong Tea (Classic Expression).High-Mountain Oolong: Ball-rolled style from high elevations, creating a thicker, creamier mouthfeel.
Oolong Tea (Classic Expression).Dong Ding Oolong (Modern Style): Modern, lightly roasted interpretations that focus on a fresh, floral character.
Oolong Tea (Classic Expression).Jade Oolong: A common commercial name for any lightly oxidized Cui Yu oolong.

Black Tea (Aromatic Expression).Jade Black Tea: A smooth black tea with notes of lychee and honey, retaining a floral background.

Experimental & Boutique Styles.White Tea: Creates a delicate tea with soft, sweet notes of hay and wildflowers.
Experimental & Boutique Styles.Green Tea: Rare, yields a brisk, vegetal tea where the floral notes are more subdued.

sensory.aroma: Intense Magnolia, Gardenia, Lily, Fresh Cream
sensory.flavor: Sugarcane, Buttery, Clean vegetal finish, hint of Lychee
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Viscous, smooth, and full-bodied with very low astringency. The liquor is a bright, pale yellow-green to light gold.

da-hong-pao.description: 'Big Red Robe'. The most legendary and revered of all Wuyi Rock Oolongs. While the name refers to a few specific mother trees, most Da Hong Pao on the market is a masterful blend of other high-quality Wuyi cultivars (like Rou Gui and Shui Xian) made in the DHP style. It is the benchmark for the complex 'rock rhyme' (Yan Yun)—a unique mineral taste and texture derived from its rocky terroir.

da-ye-zhong.description: 'Big Leaf Variety'. This is not a single cultivar, but the broad-leaf botanical varietal, Camellia sinensis var. assamica, native to Yunnan. It is the genetic mother of all Yunnan tea and is known for its robustness, powerful flavor, and suitability for fermentation and aging. It is the raw material for both Pu'er and Dian Hong black tea.
da-ye-zhong.plantType: Can grow into a large, ancient tree (gushu) or be cultivated as a bush (Camellia sinensis var. assamica).
da-ye-zhong.environment: Thrives in the subtropical, mountainous, and biodiverse environment of Yunnan Province, with many distinct regional terroirs (e.g., Yiwu, Bulang, Lincang).
da-ye-zhong.processing: This varietal's large, robust leaves are rich in polyphenols, making them ideal for the microbial fermentation of Pu'er tea and for creating complex, malty black teas. They can withstand significant processing.
da-ye-zhong.oxidation: Oxidation varies dramatically by style. Sheng Pu'er is essentially an unoxidized (0%) sun-dried green tea. Dian Hong and Shu Pu'er are fully oxidized (100%).
da-ye-zhong.roasting: Roasting is generally not a feature. Sheng Pu'er is sun-dried. Dian Hong is dried with hot air. Shu Pu'er is dried after its fermentation pile is complete.
da-ye-zhong.versatility: Extremely versatile. As a foundational varietal, it is the basis for Yunnan's most famous and diverse tea styles, from green (Pu'er) to black (Dian Hong).

china: Also found in neighboring Myanmar, Laos, Vietnam, and Thailand

Pu'er Tea.Sheng (Raw) Pu'er: Sun-dried green tea pressed into cakes for aging. Young, it's floral and astringent; aged, it's deep, woody, and complex.
Pu'er Tea.Shu (Ripe) Pu'er: Artificially fermented to mimic aging, resulting in a dark, earthy, and smooth tea.

Black Tea.Dian Hong: A fully oxidized black tea known for its malty, sweet potato, and chocolate notes, often with beautiful golden tips.

sensory.aroma: Highly variable: floral, fruity, hay (Sheng Pu'er); earthy, loamy, dark chocolate (Shu Pu'er); malty, cacao, sweet potato (Dian Hong)
sensory.flavor: Robust, complex, often with a pleasant bitterness that transforms into sweetness (huigan).
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Generally thick, full-bodied, and powerful. The liquor can be pale gold (young Sheng) to opaque black (Shu).

da-yeh-oolong.description: 'Big Leaf Oolong'. This refers to a large-leaf Assamica varietal that has been cultivated in Taiwan for over a century. While not as famous for oolong as the small-leaf sinensis varieties, it can be crafted into a unique, full-bodied oolong. Its most important role, however, was as the genetic foundation for Taiwan's modern black tea breeding programs, including being a parent of Hong Yu #18.
da-yeh-oolong.plantType: Large, robust bush or tree with large, drooping leaves (Camellia sinensis var. assamica).
da-yeh-oolong.environment: Thrives in the hot, humid, and sunny low-altitude regions of eastern Taiwan.
da-yeh-oolong.processing: As an Assamica varietal, its leaves are rich in polyphenols, making them ideal for full oxidation. They are robust and can withstand heavy rolling to break down cell walls and encourage a strong, malty flavor.
da-yeh-oolong.oxidation: When made into black tea, it undergoes full oxidation (100%). When made into oolong, it requires heavy oxidation (50-70%) to tame its natural astringency.
da-yeh-oolong.roasting: No roasting. The tea is typically dried with hot air.
da-yeh-oolong.versatility: Primarily used for black tea. While it can be made into a niche oolong, its chemical composition and leaf structure are perfectly suited for producing strong, malty black tea.

Oolong Tea (Niche).Da Yeh Oolong: A rare style of oolong with a unique, robust, and often fruity character.

Black Tea.Taiwanese Assam: Its primary use, creating a classic, robust black tea with a malty and sweet flavor, similar to Indian Assam.

sensory.aroma: Malty, fruity, honey (as black tea); ripe fruit, woody (as oolong)
sensory.flavor: Strong, robust, and sweet with a malty character.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Very full-bodied and thick with a strong presence. The liquor is a deep red (black tea) or dark amber (oolong).

fo-shou.description: 'Buddha's Hand'. A large-leaf cultivar with origins in Yongchun, Fujian, that is also cultivated in Taiwan. It is named for its unusually large leaves, which resemble a Buddha's hand citron. In Taiwan, it is most famously used to create a distinct style of traditionally crafted, heavily roasted oolong in the Muzha area.
fo-shou.plantType: Large, sprawling bush with very large, broad, and dark green leaves (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
fo-shou.environment: Grows well in the mid-elevation, humid environments of northern and central Taiwan.
fo-shou.processing: The large leaves of Fo Shou contain a lot of water and require a long, slow withering process. Their size and substance make them ideal for withstanding the stress of heavy oxidation and deep, slow roasting.
fo-shou.oxidation: Undergoes heavy oxidation (50-60%) to develop a deep, fruity, and honey-like flavor base that serves as the perfect canvas for roasting.
fo-shou.roasting: Very well-suited to heavy roasting. The traditional Muzha style involves multiple, slow bakes over charcoal, which builds immense depth, removes all astringency, and creates a signature caramel-like sweetness.
fo-shou.versatility: Specialized for traditional, heavily roasted oolongs. Its large leaf structure is not well-suited for light, 'green' oolong styles.

Traditional Oolong.Muzha Fo Shou: Its most famous Taiwanese expression. A heavily oxidized and deeply roasted oolong with a unique fruity, honeyed, and roasted character.
Traditional Oolong.Yongchun Fo Shou (Anxi): The original mainland China style, known for its strong ripe fruit notes.

sensory.aroma: Ripe Quince, Pear, Honey, Caramel, gentle roast
sensory.flavor: Thick, fruity, and sweet with a distinct, comforting roasted depth.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Exceptionally thick, viscous, and soupy with a very smooth, comforting texture. The liquor is a deep, dark amber.

fuding-da-bai.description: 'Fuding Big White'. The premier cultivar of Chinese white tea, Fuding Da Bai is the genetic backbone of the world's most famous white teas, including Silver Needle. It is celebrated for its large, fleshy buds that are covered in a thick layer of silvery-white down, which produce a tea that is exceptionally delicate, sweet, and clean.
fuding-da-bai.plantType: Vigorous, large, early-sprouting bush with good cold resistance (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
fuding-da-bai.environment: Prefers the mild, humid, and foggy coastal climate of Fuding, where the sea breezes and misty conditions are ideal for the slow withering process of white tea.
fuding-da-bai.processing: The entire philosophy of processing this cultivar is minimalism. The goal is to preserve the natural state of the leaf with as little human intervention as possible. The thick, downy buds are key to its character.
fuding-da-bai.oxidation: Oxidation is natural and very minimal (<5%), occurring slowly during the extended withering phase. There is no 'kill-green' step, allowing for a slight enzymatic change that develops its sweetness.
fuding-da-bai.roasting: No roasting is involved. The tea is simply withered (in the sun or indoors depending on weather) and then gently dried at a low temperature to remove the final moisture.
fuding-da-bai.versatility: Primarily specialized for white tea, where it is the undisputed champion. While it can be made into a simple black tea, its structure and flavor are best expressed through the gentle processing of white tea.

china: Fujian Province (Fuding, and surrounding areas like Xiapu, Fu'an)
Other provinces have tried to plant it, but Fuding is its authentic home.

White Tea.Silver Needle (Bai Hao Yin Zhen): The highest grade, made exclusively from the unopened buds of this cultivar, yielding a very delicate and sweet tea.
White Tea.White Peony (Bai Mu Dan): Made from the bud and top two leaves, resulting in a fuller-bodied tea with more complexity.

Black Tea.Fuding Black Tea: Can be processed into a sweet and mellow black tea, though this is less common.

sensory.aroma: Delicate notes of hay, fresh melon, apricot, and a subtle floral sweetness
sensory.flavor: Clean, mellow, and naturally sweet with very low bitterness or astringency.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Smooth, light, and refreshing with a clean, soft texture. The liquor is a very pale, silvery-yellow.

goko.description: 'Enlightenment'. A classic and elite cultivar from Uji, Kyoto, Goko is one of the most important traditional cultivars for producing the highest grades of Gyokuro and Matcha. It is celebrated for its ability to develop an intense, profound, and savory 'umami' flavor when shaded, creating the archetypal 'brothy' character of Uji Gyokuro.

gui-hua-xiang.description: 'Osmanthus Fragrance'. A classic and beloved Phoenix Dan Cong oolong fragrance type. It is celebrated for its delicate, elegant, and very clear aroma of sweet osmanthus flowers. It is less overwhelmingly powerful than Mi Lan Xiang, offering a more refined and purely floral experience.
gui-hua-xiang.plantType: Medium-sized Dan Cong arbor (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
gui-hua-xiang.environment: Grows in the high-altitude, misty environment of the Phoenix Mountains, which allows for the slow development of its delicate aromatic compounds.
gui-hua-xiang.processing: delicate fragrance without introducing any heavier

Dan Cong Oolong.Gui Hua Xiang Dan Cong: A medium-oxidized and lightly roasted Dan Cong, with processing focused on preserving its pure, singular osmanthus flower aroma.

hong-yu.description: 'Ruby'. Taiwan's most famous and unique black tea, Hong Yu is a modern hybrid developed by TRES. It is celebrated for its truly singular and powerful aroma, a complex bouquet of cinnamon, wintergreen, and mint, layered over a rich, malty base. It is a world-class black tea that has become an icon of the Taiwanese tea industry.
hong-yu.plantType: Vigorous, large-leaf bush with a strong upright growth habit.
hong-yu.environment: Prefers the warm, extremely humid, and stable climate around Sun Moon Lake, which mimics the conditions needed by its Assamica parentage.
hong-yu.processing: The processing is a relatively standard black tea method (wither, roll, oxidize, dry), but the magic is in the unique genetics of the leaf itself. The goal is simply to fully express the inherent character of the cultivar.
hong-yu.oxidation: Undergoes full and complete oxidation (100%) to develop the deep red color and the complex aromatic compounds that define it.
hong-yu.roasting: No roasting. The tea is dried with hot air to halt oxidation and reduce moisture content. All of its flavor comes from the leaf chemistry and oxidation.
hong-yu.versatility: Completely specialized. Hong Yu was bred for the express purpose of making a world-class black tea, and its unique genetics make it unsuitable for other styles.

taiwan: Nantou County (Yuchi Township - Sun Moon Lake)

Black Tea.Ruby #18 Black Tea: Its sole, iconic expression. A fully oxidized black tea with a powerful and unmistakable spicy-minty aroma and a rich, sweet flavor.

sensory.aroma: Powerful Cinnamon, Wintergreen, Mint, Camphor, Malt
sensory.flavor: Malty, sweet, with a complex spice character and a unique cooling sensation in the finish.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Full-bodied, robust, and very smooth with a long, powerful, and cooling aftertaste. The liquor is a brilliant, clear ruby red.

hong-yun.description: 'Red Rhyme'. Another modern black tea masterpiece from TRES, Hong Yun was developed to have a more fruit-forward and floral profile compared to Hong Yu's spicy character. It is known for its bright, uplifting aroma of citrus fruits like yuzu and orange peel, combined with a sweet, lingering floral finish.
hong-yun.plantType: Vigorous bush, slightly smaller and more compact than Hong Yu.
hong-yun.environment: Grows well in the warm, humid environment of Yuchi (Sun Moon Lake) and other black tea producing regions in Taiwan.
hong-yun.processing: Like Hong Yu, the processing is a standard black tea method. The skill of the tea master lies in perfectly timing the oxidation to capture the peak of its citrus and floral aromatics.
hong-yun.oxidation: Undergoes full oxidation (100%) to develop its bright red liquor and complex fruity-floral flavor profile.
hong-yun.roasting: No roasting. The tea is dried with hot air. Its flavor is derived from its unique parentage and the oxidation process.
hong-yun.versatility: Completely specialized. Hong Yun was specifically bred to create a unique, aromatic black tea and is not used for other tea styles.

taiwan: Nantou County (Yuchi Township - Sun Moon Lake)

Black Tea.Hong Yun Black Tea: Its only expression. A fully oxidized black tea designed to be exceptionally aromatic, with a focus on bright citrus and floral notes.

sensory.aroma: Bright Yuzu, Orange Peel, Passionfruit, underlying floral sweetness
sensory.flavor: Citrusy, sweet, and vibrant with a clean, honey-like finish.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Medium-to-full-bodied, smooth, and very aromatic with a long, sweet aftertaste. The liquor is a bright orange-red.

huang-guan-yin.description: 'Yellow Goddess'. A successful modern hybrid cultivar, created by crossing Huang Jin Gui (for aroma) and Tie Guan Yin (for substance). It is an intensely aromatic tea, often presenting a bouquet of powerful floral notes like gardenia and magnolia, and has become a popular 'new style' of Wuyi Rock Oolong.
huang-guan-yin.plantType: Vigorous, productive, early-sprouting hybrid bush (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
huang-guan-yin.environment: Bred to be vigorous and adaptable, it is grown in both Anxi and Wuyi. In Wuyi, the rocky terroir adds a mineral foundation to its powerful aroma.
huang-guan-yin.processing: This cultivar was designed for aroma, so the entire processing chain is geared towards preserving its highly volatile floral compounds. Gentle handling is key.
huang-guan-yin.oxidation: Oxidation is kept on the lighter side for an oolong (20-40%) to maintain the freshness and vibrancy of its floral character.
huang-guan-yin.roasting: Roasting, especially for the Yancha style, must be very light and at a low temperature. It is more of a finishing bake to stabilize the tea. A heavy roast would completely destroy the delicate aroma it was bred to produce.
huang-guan-yin.versatility: Moderately versatile. It can be crafted into either a Wuyi or Anxi style, but it will always be a light, intensely fragrant oolong. It lacks the structure for heavy roasting or black tea production.

Wuyi Rock Oolong (New Style).Huang Guan Yin Yancha: A very lightly roasted Yancha where the processing is designed to maximize its explosive floral aroma.

Anxi Oolong (Green Style).Fragrant Anxi Oolong: When processed in Anxi, it is made into a very green, unroasted oolong similar to modern Tie Guan Yin, but even more aromatic.

sensory.aroma: Intense Gardenia, Ginger Lily, Magnolia, very perfume-like
sensory.flavor: Sweet, overwhelmingly floral, with a light body and a clean finish. When from Wuyi, it has a subtle mineral undertone.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Smooth and silky, generally lighter-bodied than traditional Yancha. The liquor is a very bright, pale golden-yellow.

huang-jin-gui.description: 'Golden Osmanthus'. A classic Anxi oolong celebrated for its singular, intense, and unmistakable aroma of sweet osmanthus flowers. It is an early-budding and high-yielding cultivar, prized for its ability to produce a light, crisp, and almost perfume-like tea that serves as a benchmark for pure floral aroma.
huang-jin-gui.plantType: Early-budding, productive, spreading bush (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
huang-jin-gui.environment: Thrives in the Hukou area of Anxi county, where the specific terroir is said to produce the most fragrant expression of the cultivar.
huang-jin-gui.processing: The processing of Huang Jin Gui is a race against time to capture its volatile aromatics. The leaves are delicate and require gentle handling and a short processing window.
huang-jin-gui.oxidation: Oxidation is very light (10-20%), just enough to eliminate the green, grassy notes and allow the powerful osmanthus fragrance to fully emerge.
huang-jin-gui.roasting: Completely unroasted, aside from a final low-temperature bake for drying and stabilization. Any significant roasting would erase its signature character.
huang-jin-gui.versatility: Not versatile at all. Huang Jin Gui is a master of a single craft: producing an intensely aromatic, light-bodied green oolong. Its entire value is based on this specialization.

Anxi Oolong (Light & Aromatic).Huang Jin Gui Oolong: This is its one and only famous expression. It is processed as a very green, unroasted oolong to capture its fleeting, powerful osmanthus fragrance at its peak.

sensory.aroma: Overwhelming sweet Osmanthus, perfume-like, fresh flowers
sensory.flavor: Light, crisp, sweet, and intensely floral with a clean, brisk finish.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Relatively thin-bodied and delicate with no astringency. The liquor is a very pale, clear golden-yellow.

huangshan-qunti-zhong.description: 'Huangshan Population'. The local, genetically diverse heirloom population of tea plants from the famous Huangshan (Yellow Mountain) scenic area. This is the authentic material for creating Huangshan Maofeng, a beloved green tea known for its light, sweet, and refreshingly floral character, often with notes of magnolia.
huangshan-qunti-zhong.plantType: Variable growth habits due to genetic diversity; typically medium-sized bushes (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
huangshan-qunti-zhong.environment: Grows at high altitudes (700-800m) in the cloudy, misty, and cool environment of Huangshan. The rich soil and constant cloud cover create a very sweet and tender leaf.
huangshan-qunti-zhong.processing: The processing of Huangshan Maofeng is simpler than many famous teas. After a short withering, the leaves undergo a 'kill-green' and shaping process in a large pan, followed by a careful baking process to dry.
huangshan-qunti-zhong.oxidation: Zero oxidation. The 'kill-green' step is done quickly after harvest to lock in the fresh, vegetal and floral notes of the leaf.
huangshan-qunti-zhong.roasting: The key step is a low-temperature bake ('hong bei'). Unlike the high heat of pan-firing, this gentle baking process slowly removes moisture while preserving the tea's delicate floral aroma and natural sweetness.
huangshan-qunti-zhong.versatility: Completely specialized. This heirloom population is used exclusively to make the sweet, floral green tea known as Huangshan Maofeng.

china: Anhui Province (Huangshan - particularly the areas around Taohua Feng (Peach Blossom Peak))

Green Tea.Huangshan Maofeng: Its sole expression. A gently processed green tea consisting of a bud and one or two leaves. It is lightly baked rather than pan-fired, preserving a fresh, floral character.

sensory.aroma: Fresh cut grass, elegant floral notes like Magnolia and Orchid
sensory.flavor: Naturally sweet, light, and refreshing with no bitterness and a clean, long-lasting floral aftertaste.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Smooth, light, and mellow with a very clean texture. The liquor is a clear, pale apricot color.

inzatsu-131.description: An old and unique Japanese cultivar that is a hybrid of an Assamica variety and a native Zairai. It is known for its exotic, almost foreign aroma that is highly floral and sometimes spicy, reminiscent of teas from Darjeeling or Taiwan. It is a rare cultivar, prized by connoisseurs for its unique character.
inzatsu-131.environment: Well-suited to the climate of Shizuoka where it was developed.
inzatsu-131.processing: Processing Inzatsu 131 aims to highlight its unique, non-Japanese aroma. The method can be adapted to push it towards a greener or a more oxidized style depending on the tea maker's goal.
inzatsu-131.oxidation: Oxidation can vary. As a Sencha, it is unoxidized. However, it is often allowed a slight oxidation (like an oolong) to further develop its exotic floral and spicy notes.
inzatsu-131.roasting: Roasting is typically light to preserve its unique aroma.
inzatsu-131.versatility: Highly versatile. Its unique hybrid genetics make it a rare cultivar that can be successfully crafted into a wide range of styles, from a unique green tea to a fragrant oolong or black tea.

Sencha.Exotic Sencha: When made as a green tea, it has a powerful, exotic floral aroma unlike any other Sencha.

Japanese Black/Oolong.Aromatic Teas: Its Assamica lineage makes it an excellent candidate for producing highly aromatic, lightly oxidized oolongs or even full black teas.

sensory.aroma: Exotic flowers, spicy, muscatel, sometimes a hint of citrus
sensory.flavor: Aromatic, slightly spicy, with a unique floral sweetness.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Smooth and medium-bodied with a very fragrant and lasting finish. The liquor is often a deeper golden-yellow.

jin-xuan.description: 'Golden Lily'. A celebrated modern cultivar developed by Taiwan's TRES in 1981, it is famous for its distinct, natural 'nai xiang' or 'milk fragrance'. This creamy, buttery, and smooth profile, combined with its high yield and adaptability, has made Jin Xuan one of the most popular and beloved teas in Taiwan and beyond.
jin-xuan.plantType: Vigorous, adaptable, high-yielding bush with distinctive round, thick leaves (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
jin-xuan.environment: Highly adaptable, thriving in a wide range of environments from lower elevations in Nantou to high altitudes on Alishan (200-1,600m).
jin-xuan.processing: The processing for Jin Xuan oolong is specifically designed to highlight its unique, inherent 'nai xiang' (milk fragrance). Careful withering is key to developing this signature trait.
jin-xuan.oxidation: For oolong, oxidation is light (15-25%) to preserve the creamy notes. For black tea, it undergoes full oxidation (100%), which transforms the creaminess into a honeyed sweetness.
jin-xuan.roasting: Typically unroasted for the classic Milk Oolong style to maintain its fresh, creamy character.
jin-xuan.versatility: Very versatile. It is a star performer as a light oolong and also makes an exceptionally smooth and sweet black tea, making it a valuable and flexible cultivar for farmers.

Oolong Tea.Milk Oolong: Its most famous expression. A lightly oxidized, ball-rolled oolong with a prominent creamy, milky, and buttery character.

Black Tea.Jin Xuan Black Tea: When fully oxidized, it produces a uniquely sweet and smooth black tea with notes of honey and a hint of its signature creaminess.

sensory.aroma: Distinct Milk, Cream, Butter, light floral (Osmanthus)
sensory.flavor: Buttery, smooth, sweet, with a clean and light finish.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Smooth, creamy, and round with very low astringency. The liquor is a bright, pale golden color.

ju-duo-zai.description: 'Saw-leaf'. A rare, old-grove Dan Cong varietal from the Phoenix Mountains, named for the sharply serrated, saw-like edges of its leaves. It is a rustic and powerful tea, known for its wild, herbal, and stone fruit character, representing an older, less-manicured style of Dan Cong.
ju-duo-zai.plantType: Medium-sized Dan Cong arbor with distinctive, sharply serrated leaves (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
ju-duo-zai.environment: Grows in the old tea gardens of the Phoenix Mountains, often from trees that are quite old. The specific terroir contributes to its rustic and deep flavor.
ju-duo-zai.processing: Processing this old-grove varietal follows traditional methods. The tea master aims to capture the full, complex character of the leaves rather than targeting a single, narrow fragrance profile.
ju-duo-zai.oxidation: Undergoes a medium-to-heavy oxidation (40-55%) to develop its deep fruit notes and complex, rustic flavor base.
ju-duo-zai.roasting: Typically receives a medium charcoal roast to integrate its powerful flavors, add depth, and ensure the tea will age well.
ju-duo-zai.versatility: Highly specialized. Ju Duo Zai is a specific, old-style Dan Cong oolong appreciated for its rustic power and complexity.

Dan Cong Oolong.Ju Duo Zai Dan Cong: A traditionally processed Dan Cong oolong where the processing aims to express its wild, deep, and untamed character.

sensory.aroma: Wild herbs, stone fruit (apricot), honey, wet stone
sensory.flavor: Rustic, deep, and mineralic with a complex, slightly wild sweetness and a powerful finish.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Thick, full-bodied, and powerful, often with a noticeable energetic character. The liquor is a deep golden-amber.

kanayamidori.description: A mid-budding cultivar known for its distinctive, slightly sweet, and milky or vanilla-like aroma. It is a popular choice for both Sencha and Fukamushi Sencha, and its unique fragrance also makes it a favorite for producing aromatic, lightly roasted Hojicha.

kirari-31.description: A very new Japanese green tea cultivar registered in 2015. It was bred for its high resistance to disease and its suitability for producing a very fragrant and low-astringency Kamairicha (pan-fired green tea). It is known for its bright, clear liquor and a sweet, slightly milky, and floral aroma.
kirari-31.plantType: Early-budding, vigorous bush with excellent disease resistance (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
kirari-31.environment: Thrives in the warm climates of southern Japan, particularly in regions that specialize in Kamairicha production.
kirari-31.processing: Kirari 31 was specifically bred with pan-firing in mind. Its chemical composition responds well to the high, dry heat of this method, creating a fragrant tea without developing bitterness.
kirari-31.oxidation: Zero oxidation. The 'kill-green' step, whether by pan-firing or steaming, is done immediately after harvest.
kirari-31.roasting: For its primary style, Kamairicha, the pan-firing serves as the 'roast', creating a gentle nutty character. For Sencha, it would receive a standard light final bake.
kirari-31.versatility: Moderately versatile. While it excels as a pan-fired tea, it can also produce a high-quality steamed Sencha, making it a valuable modern cultivar.

Kamairicha (Pan-Fired Green Tea).Aromatic Kamairicha: Its premier expression. The pan-firing process highlights its sweet, floral aroma and results in a very bright, clean tea.

Sencha.Aromatic Sencha: Can also be steamed to make a fragrant Sencha, though this is less common.

sensory.aroma: Sweet, floral, slightly milky
sensory.flavor: Very low astringency with a clear, lasting sweetness and a clean finish.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Smooth and medium-bodied with a very refreshing texture. The liquor is a bright, clear green-yellow.

komakage.description: An excellent shading cultivar from Aichi prefecture, known for its strong, upright growth and resistance to cold. It produces a high-quality Tencha for Matcha with a good balance of umami and a unique, slightly savory, almost spicy character that distinguishes it from the classic Uji cultivars.
komakage.plantType: Vigorous, upright bush with strong cold resistance (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
komakage.environment: Very well-suited to the climate of Aichi and other regions that experience colder winters than southern Japan.
komakage.processing: Komakage is well-suited for shaded cultivation. Its robust nature makes it a reliable choice for farmers. It is processed into Tencha for Matcha production.
komakage.oxidation: Zero oxidation. The leaves are steamed promptly after being harvested from the shaded plants.
komakage.roasting: No roasting. As Tencha, the leaves are dried flat in a special oven without being rolled to prepare them for stone-milling.
komakage.versatility: Highly specialized for Matcha. It is a key cultivar for Matcha production outside of the Uji region, particularly in Aichi.

Matcha & Tencha.Nishio Matcha: It is a cornerstone cultivar for Matcha from the Nishio region, prized for its unique flavor profile and reliability.

sensory.aroma: Savory greens, hint of spice
sensory.flavor: Good umami with a unique, slightly spicy or savory character and a clean finish.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Smooth and full-bodied, creating a satisfying bowl of Matcha. The liquor is a deep, strong green.

koshun.description: 'Fragrance of Shizuoka'. A remarkable modern cultivar bred specifically for its astonishingly powerful and unique floral aroma. It produces a Sencha with a perfume-like fragrance reminiscent of lily-of-the-valley, jasmine, and cherry leaves, offering a completely different experience from classic, umami-focused Japanese green teas.
koshun.plantType: Upright, vigorous bush with long, elegant leaves (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
koshun.environment: Well-suited to the climate of Shizuoka, where it was developed.
koshun.processing: Processing Koshun is all about capturing its volatile aromatic compounds. It is typically lightly steamed (Asamushi) to prevent the heat from damaging the delicate floral notes. Careful, low-temperature drying is also crucial.
koshun.oxidation: Zero oxidation for the Sencha style. The leaves are steamed immediately to lock in the floral aroma.
koshun.roasting: A very gentle, low-temperature final drying roast is used to avoid baking away the prized floral fragrance.
koshun.versatility: Moderately versatile. While its primary use is for a unique style of aromatic Sencha, its genetics also make it suitable for crafting fragrant Japanese oolongs.

Sencha.Aromatic Sencha: Its primary expression. A lightly steamed green tea where processing is entirely focused on preserving its unique, intense floral bouquet.

Japanese Oolong.Light Oolong: Its aromatic potential also makes it a great candidate for producing lightly oxidized Japanese oolongs.

sensory.aroma: Intense lily-of-the-valley, jasmine, cherry leaf, very perfume-like
sensory.flavor: Light-bodied, highly aromatic, with a sweet, floral taste and a clean, fragrant finish.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Smooth and light with very low astringency. The liquor is a very pale, bright green-yellow.

liu-an-gua-pian.description: 'Lu'an Melon Slice'. A unique and famous Chinese green tea from Anhui, notable for what it lacks: it is made entirely from mature leaves, with all buds and stems meticulously removed. The finished tea, resembling melon seeds, is baked, not pan-fired, giving it a complex, toasty, and vegetal flavor.
liu-an-gua-pian.plantType: Hardy, medium-sized bushes from the local heirloom population (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
liu-an-gua-pian.environment: Grows in the hilly, temperate climate of Lu'an City in western Anhui, particularly in the Qishan mountain range.
liu-an-gua-pian.processing: The processing is unique. After picking, the leaves are de-stemmed and de-veined by hand. They are then wok-fired to kill-green and shape, followed by a multi-stage, slow baking process over charcoal fires, which is crucial for developing its flavor.
liu-an-gua-pian.oxidation: Zero oxidation. The leaves undergo a rapid 'kill-green' in a wok to halt all enzymatic processes.
liu-an-gua-pian.roasting: Roasting is the defining characteristic. The tea is baked multiple times over charcoal fires of varying intensity. This 'lao huo' (old fire) process builds a deep, complex, and toasty flavor without any smokiness.
liu-an-gua-pian.versatility: Extremely specialized. This cultivar and its unique processing method (no buds/stems, baked) are inseparable from the identity of Liu An Gua Pian.

china: Anhui Province (Lu'an City, specifically Jinzhai and Yu'an districts)

Green Tea (Baked).Liu An Gua Pian: Its sole expression. A baked green tea made from single, de-stemmed mature leaves, which are shaped and repeatedly baked over charcoal fires.

sensory.aroma: Toasty, sweet corn, vegetal, hint of floral high notes
sensory.flavor: Complex, rich, and mellow with a balance of toasted and fresh vegetal flavors, and a very smooth, sweet finish.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Thick, rich, and smooth with a very satisfying, full texture. The liquor is a clear, bright greenish-yellow.

long-jing-43.description: 'Long Jing No. 43'. The most widespread and commercially important modern cultivar for producing West Lake Long Jing tea. It was developed for its high yield, beautiful appearance, and early budding time, allowing for the prized pre-Qingming harvest. It produces the classic, beloved nutty and sweet soybean flavor of Long Jing.
long-jing-43.plantType: Compact, early-sprouting bush with high productivity (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
long-jing-43.environment: Thrives in the temperate climate and sandy loam soil of the hills surrounding Hangzhou's West Lake, though it is highly adaptable and grown elsewhere.
long-jing-43.processing: Processing is defined by the pan-firing ('chao qing') step. The tender leaves are skillfully pressed against the hot surface of a wok to stop oxidation, dry the leaves, and shape them into their iconic flat form.
long-jing-43.oxidation: Zero oxidation. As a green tea, the leaves are heated (in this case, pan-fired) almost immediately after harvesting to deactivate the enzymes responsible for oxidation.
long-jing-43.roasting: No roasting. The 'roasty' notes in Long Jing come directly from the pan-firing process itself, not from a separate roasting step.
long-jing-43.versatility: Specialized for pan-fired green tea. Its entire set of desirable traits—early budding, tender leaves, beautiful shape—is geared towards producing high-quality Long Jing.

china: Other green tea regions across China

Green Tea.West Lake Long Jing: This is its premier expression. The leaves are pan-fired in a wok to halt oxidation and create their signature flat shape and toasted flavor.

Other Green Teas.Various pan-fired styles: Its reliability makes it a choice for producing other flat-style green teas outside of Hangzhou.

sensory.aroma: Toasted Chestnut, Sweet Soybean, Fresh Grass
sensory.flavor: Nutty, mellow, savory (umami), and subtly sweet with no bitterness.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Smooth, mellow, and soft with a clean, refreshing finish. The liquor is a bright, clear yellow-green.

long-jing-qunti-zhong.description: 'Long Jing Population'. This is not a single clonal cultivar but the original, genetically diverse, seed-propagated heirloom population of Long Jing tea plants. Connoisseurs often prefer it to the modern #43 clone, believing it to have a deeper, more complex, and nuanced flavor profile, though its appearance is less uniform and it buds later.
long-jing-qunti-zhong.plantType: Variable, seed-propagated bushes with diverse growth habits (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
long-jing-qunti-zhong.environment: Grows in the core, traditional production areas around West Lake in Hangzhou. It is perfectly adapted to this specific terroir over centuries of growth.
long-jing-qunti-zhong.processing: The processing is identical to Long Jing #43 (pan-firing), but the skill of the tea master is even more crucial due to the variability in leaf size and moisture content from the genetically diverse bushes.
long-jing-qunti-zhong.oxidation: Zero oxidation. Like all Long Jing, it is a green tea where oxidation is halted immediately by pan-firing.
long-jing-qunti-zhong.roasting: No roasting. The complex toasted notes are a direct result of the skillful pan-firing process.
long-jing-qunti-zhong.versatility: Specialized for pan-fired green tea. It represents the historical and most complex expression of the Long Jing style.

china: Zhejiang Province (Hangou - core West Lake scenic area)

Green Tea.West Lake Long Jing (Heirloom): The most traditional and complex expression of Long Jing. It is pan-fired in the same way as #43, but its genetic diversity yields a multi-layered flavor.

sensory.aroma: Deeper and more complex than #43, with floral and fruity notes mixed in with the classic chestnut and soybean
sensory.flavor: Multi-layered, nuanced, rich, with a longer and more complex aftertaste (huigan).
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Often thicker and fuller-bodied than #43, with a very smooth and satisfying texture. The liquor is a rich yellow-green.

mao-xie.description: 'Hairy Crab'. An Anxi oolong cultivar named for the fine, downy hairs on its fresh leaves and the slightly curled shape of the brewed leaf, thought to resemble a crab. It is known for its forward, fruity-floral aroma, high yield, and early budding, making it a commercially important variety in Anxi.
mao-xie.plantType: Semi-spreading bush with dense branches and high productivity (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
mao-xie.environment: Highly adaptable and vigorous, growing well in the general terroir of Anxi County, from lower to mid-elevations.
mao-xie.processing: Mao Xie is prized for its upfront aroma which can be easily developed. The processing focuses on a controlled withering to bring out these volatile compounds without needing the heavy bruising or roasting that other cultivars require.
mao-xie.oxidation: Undergoes light oxidation (15-25%) to preserve its characteristic fresh and fruity notes. The processing is efficient and focuses on capturing the peak aroma.
mao-xie.roasting: Like Ben Shan, it is almost always unroasted or receives only a minimal drying bake to preserve its fresh, fragrant profile.
mao-xie.versatility: Similar to Ben Shan, it has low versatility. It is a specialist in producing fragrant, accessible, and affordable green-style oolongs and does not have the structure for other tea styles.

Oolong Tea (Classic Expression).Anxi Oolong (Aromatic Style): Made in the modern 'green' style, similar to Ben Shan. The processing is designed to highlight its forward, almost perfume-like fruity and floral character.

sensory.aroma: Fruity-floral, Green Apple, Apricot, Fresh Flowers
sensory.flavor: Bright, sweet, and very aromatic with a pleasant, light character.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Medium-bodied with a smooth texture and a distinctly fragrant finish. The liquor is a bright golden-yellow.

mei-zhan.description: A highly versatile Fujian cultivar, originally from Anxi. While it can be made into a pleasant oolong, it has gained modern fame as one of the primary cultivars used to produce Jin Jun Mei, an elite, bud-only black tea from the Wuyi region. Its inherent sweetness and fruity notes make it an excellent base for high-end black teas.
mei-zhan.plantType: Vigorous, semi-arbor type with good adaptability (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
mei-zhan.environment: Highly adaptable to different terroirs within Fujian, which has contributed to its widespread use.
mei-zhan.processing: Mei Zhan's versatility is due to its balanced chemical composition. Its buds are particularly well-suited for black tea processing, as they are rich in compounds that create sweetness and a thick texture when fully oxidized.
mei-zhan.oxidation: Oxidation is typically full (100%) for its most famous black tea expression. When made as an oolong, it undergoes medium oxidation (30-40%).
mei-zhan.roasting: Roasting is not a key feature. Black tea expressions are simply dried. Oolong expressions may receive a light bake.
mei-zhan.versatility: Extremely versatile. It is a rare cultivar that can be skillfully crafted into high-quality oolong, black, and even white tea, though its modern fame is overwhelmingly tied to black tea.

china: Other provinces like Zhejiang and Sichuan

Black Tea.Jin Jun Mei: Its most prestigious modern use. The tender buds are crafted into a high-end black tea with notes of honey, fruit, and sweet potato.

Oolong Tea.Mei Zhan Oolong: Can be made into a fragrant Anxi-style or Wuyi-style oolong, though this is less common now.

White Tea.Mei Zhan Buds: Its downy buds can be processed into a sweet, fruity white tea.

sensory.aroma: Honey, sweet potato, fruity (as black tea); Floral, fruity (as oolong)
sensory.flavor: Very sweet, mellow, and complex with a smooth finish and no astringency.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Smooth, full, and often thick and syrupy, especially as Jin Jun Mei. The liquor is a beautiful golden-orange.

meiryoku.description: A late-budding cultivar known for producing a Sencha with a refreshing, slightly floral aroma and a unique, bright flavor with hints of citrus and spice. It has a very favorable chemical composition with high amino acid content and is also noted for its strong resistance to common tea plant diseases.

mengding-ganlu.description: 'Mengding Sweet Dew'. An ancient and celebrated green tea from Mengding Mountain in Sichuan, often cited as one of the oldest forms of tribute tea in China. It is known for its delicate, tightly rolled leaves covered in fine down, and a fresh, complex flavor profile that balances umami, sweetness, and a lasting floral aroma.
mengding-ganlu.plantType: Small-leaf, downy-bud cultivar, adapted to high-altitude growth (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
mengding-ganlu.environment: Grows on the perennially misty and rainy slopes of Mengding Mountain, where the constant cloud cover and rich soil create very tender and flavorful leaves.
mengding-ganlu.processing: Processing involves a sequence of pan-firing to kill-green, followed by multiple stages of intricate hand-rolling and drying. This complex rolling technique is what creates the tightly twisted shape and develops the tea's deep flavor.
mengding-ganlu.oxidation: Zero oxidation. The leaves are quickly pan-fired after harvest to halt all oxidation.
mengding-ganlu.roasting: No roasting. The tea is dried using the heat from the pan-firing and subsequent drying steps. The focus is on shape and preserving fresh flavor, not on a baked or roasted character.
mengding-ganlu.versatility: Highly specialized. The cultivar is intrinsically linked to the Mengding Ganlu style of processed green tea.

Green Tea.Mengding Ganlu: A very fine green tea made from tender buds and leaves. The processing involves a three-stage rolling and drying process to create its twisted, downy appearance and lock in its aroma.

sensory.aroma: Toasted nuts, sweet florals, fresh vegetal notes
sensory.flavor: Lasting sweetness, distinct umami, and a clean, refreshing aftertaste.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Smooth, mellow, and thick, with a rich texture from the abundant leaf hairs. The liquor is a clear, bright yellow-green.

mengku-da-ye-zhong.description: 'Mengku Big Leaf Variety'. A highly sought-after sub-variety of the Da Ye (Assamica) varietal, native to the Mengku region of Lincang, Yunnan. It is celebrated for its 'dual characteristics' of strong bitterness and powerful aroma, combined with a thick texture and an exceptionally fast and intense returning sweetness ('huigan').
mengku-da-ye-zhong.plantType: Large, robust arbor tree with large, leathery leaves that have prominent veins (Camellia sinensis var. assamica).
mengku-da-ye-zhong.environment: Grows in the high-altitude, mountainous region of Mengku, particularly around Bingdao (Ice Island), which is famous for this cultivar.
mengku-da-ye-zhong.processing: Processing is identical to other Sheng Pu'er teas: pan-firing to kill-green, rolling to shape, and crucially, sun-drying to preserve the enzymes necessary for long-term aging and fermentation.
mengku-da-ye-zhong.oxidation: Minimal oxidation (<5%) from processing, just like other Sheng Pu'er. The true transformation happens over years of aging.
mengku-da-ye-zhong.roasting: No roasting. Sun-drying is the defining and required final step before the tea is steamed and compressed into cakes.
mengku-da-ye-zhong.versatility: Extremely specialized. The Mengku Da Ye cultivar is one of the most prized materials for high-end, single-origin Sheng Pu'er.

china: Yunnan Province (Lincang Prefecture, specifically Mengku Township)

Sheng (Raw) Pu'er.Mengku Pu'er: Its exclusive expression. A powerful raw Pu'er prized for its strong character, excellent aging potential, and perfect balance of bitterness and sweetness.

sensory.aroma: Powerful and penetrating floral and honey fragrance
sensory.flavor: Initially strong and bitter, but it rapidly transforms into an intense, profound, and long-lasting sweetness (huigan).
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Thick, viscous, and powerful, with a strong energetic sensation ('cha qi'). The liquor is a bright, clear golden-yellow.

mi-lan-xiang.description: 'Honey Orchid Fragrance'. The most popular, accessible, and representative of all Phoenix Dan Cong oolongs. It is beloved for its intoxicating and forward aroma that beautifully mimics the scent of honey, orchids, and ripe stone fruit, all built upon the classic mineral-rich foundation of its mountainous terroir.
mi-lan-xiang.plantType: Tall, upright arbor type, can grow into a small tree (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
mi-lan-xiang.environment: Thrives in the high-altitude (600-1,200m), misty, and rocky environment of the Phoenix (Feng Huang) Mountains.
mi-lan-xiang.processing: The key to processing Mi Lan Xiang is the carefully controlled withering and bruising ('yao qing') stage. This is where the leaf's cell walls are broken down just enough to develop the signature honey-orchid aroma without introducing bitterness.
mi-lan-xiang.oxidation: Undergoes a medium level of oxidation (25-40%), which is the sweet spot for developing its complex fruity and floral notes while retaining a fresh vibrancy.
mi-lan-xiang.roasting: Receives a light to medium charcoal roasting. This bake helps to stabilize the tea, round out the flavors, and fix the beautiful aroma, making it more persistent over multiple infusions.
mi-lan-xiang.versatility: Specialized for the Dan Cong oolong style. While theoretically it could be processed differently, its entire value and identity lie in its famous 'honey orchid' aromatic profile.

Dan Cong Oolong.Mi Lan Xiang Dan Cong: This is its primary and most famous expression. A medium-oxidized and lightly roasted oolong designed to be explosively aromatic.

sensory.aroma: Intense Honey, Orchid, Lychee, Sweet Potato
sensory.flavor: Sweet, fruity, and floral with a distinct honeyed character and a long, vibrant finish.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Full-bodied, creamy, and smooth with a characteristic sweet and fragrant aftertaste. The liquor is a bright golden-orange.

oku-yutaka.description: 'Late Abundant'. A late-budding hybrid of Yabukita and Yutakamidori, Oku Yutaka combines the robust body of its parents with a refined, less astringent flavor. It is a high-yielding and disease-resistant cultivar, valued for producing a full-bodied Sencha with a rich flavor and a bright green color.

okuhikari.description: 'Late Light'. A late-budding cultivar with a refreshing, brisk mouthfeel and a distinct floral and woody character that sets it apart from the more common vegetal or umami-driven Senchas. It is a versatile and reliable cultivar for farmers.
okuhikari.plantType: Vigorous, late-budding bush (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
okuhikari.environment: Its late budding makes it a useful cultivar for extending the spring harvest season and avoiding frost. It is adaptable to various climates.
okuhikari.processing: Okuhikari is typically processed as a standard Sencha (Chumushi) to maintain the balance of its unique flavor profile.
okuhikari.oxidation: Zero oxidation. The leaves are steamed immediately after harvest.
okuhikari.roasting: A standard light final drying roast is applied to stabilize the tea and round out its flavors.
okuhikari.versatility: Specialized for Sencha. It offers a unique flavor profile that adds diversity to the world of Sencha.

Sencha.Refreshing Sencha: Its primary use is to produce a Sencha with a unique, brisk, and slightly woody-floral character.

sensory.aroma: Floral, woody, fresh, slightly herbaceous
sensory.flavor: Brisk, clean, and refreshing with a pleasant sweetness and a distinct character.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Smooth, light-to-medium-bodied with a very clean and uplifting finish. The liquor is a clear, bright green-yellow.

okumidori.description: 'Late Green'. A late-budding, versatile cultivar with a rich, creamy flavor, often used for Matcha or blended with Yabukita.

qi-lan.description: 'Rare Orchid' or 'Marvelous Orchid'. A highly aromatic cultivar that originated in southern Fujian but has found a second home in the Wuyi Mountains. It is celebrated for its powerful and persistent orchid-like fragrance, which it can express beautifully as both a greener Anxi-style oolong and a more robust, roasted Wuyi-style rock oolong.
qi-lan.plantType: Upright, vigorous bush with good productivity (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
qi-lan.environment: Highly adaptable, it thrives in both the clay soils of its native southern Fujian and the rocky terroir of the Wuyi Mountains.
qi-lan.processing: it undergoes a traditional Yancha process with a moderate roast. In Anxi
qi-lan.oxidation: it is processed very lightly like a modern Tie Guan Yin to preserve its fresh aroma.,Oxidation ranges from light (20-30% for Anxi style) to medium (40-50% for Wuyi style)

Wuyi Rock Oolong (Yancha).Qi Lan Yancha: When grown in Wuyi, it's made into an aroma-forward rock oolong, balancing its orchid fragrance with a mineral base and a light-to-medium roast.

Anxi Oolong.Qi Lan Oolong: When processed in Anxi, it is made in a greener, unroasted style that maximizes its intense, fresh floral aroma.

qi-men-zhong.description: 'Qimen Species'. This is not a single clone, but the local heirloom population of small-leaf tea bushes from Qimen county, Anhui. It is the one and only material used for making Keemun black tea. When processed into black tea, it produces a famously complex aroma with notes of wine, rose, pine, and dried fruit, earning it the title 'the Burgundy of tea'.
qi-men-zhong.plantType: Small-leaf, genetically diverse bushes adapted to the local terroir (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
qi-men-zhong.environment: Grows in the mild, humid, and often foggy climate of Qimen county in southern Anhui, where the soil and environment are perfect for developing its complex aromatics.
qi-men-zhong.processing: carefully controlled withering and oxidation process. This allows the full range of aromatic compounds within the Qi Men Zhong leaves to develop.,Undergoes full oxidation (100%). The oxidation process is meticulous and often takes longer than for other black teas
