china: Anhui Province (Qimen county and surrounding areas)

Black Tea.Keemun (Qimen Hongcha): Its only expression. A world-famous black tea known for its incredible aromatic complexity. Different grades exist, like Hao Ya (downy buds) and Mao Feng (pointed leaves).

qing-xin.description: 'Green Heart'. The undisputed king of Taiwanese oolongs, Qing Xin is celebrated for its ability to perfectly express the unique terroir of Taiwan's high mountains. It produces a tea with an ethereal, elegant character, a remarkably thick and creamy mouthfeel, and a delicate floral aroma of lilac and gardenia. It is the benchmark for high-end Taiwanese tea.
qing-xin.plantType: Relatively small, slow-growing bush that requires meticulous care and specific conditions to thrive (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
qing-xin.environment: Grows best at very high altitudes (1,000-2,600m) where cool temperatures, constant mist, and large diurnal temperature swings concentrate flavors in the leaves.
qing-xin.processing: Processing Qing Xin is all about preservation. The goal is to capture the pristine character of the high-mountain leaf with minimal intervention. Gentle handling and a slow, controlled withering process are essential.
qing-xin.oxidation: Undergoes very light oxidation (15-25%) to develop its creamy texture and floral notes without losing the freshness endowed by its high-altitude terroir.
qing-xin.roasting: Generally unroasted. A final, very light bake is applied for drying, but any significant roast would be seen as masking the pure, delicate character of the leaf.
qing-xin.versatility: Highly versatile for high-quality teas. It is the gold standard for High Mountain Oolong and Baozhong, and also makes an excellent Taiwanese green tea. Its quality ceiling is extremely high.

taiwan: Hsinchu (for Bi Luo Chun green tea)

High Mountain Oolong (Gao Shan Cha).Lishan/Alishan Oolong: Its highest expression. A lightly oxidized, unroasted, ball-rolled oolong with an incredibly thick, creamy body and delicate floral notes.

Baozhong Oolong.Pouchong: A lightly oxidized, twisted-leaf oolong that emphasizes its fresh floral aroma.

Green Tea.Sanxia Bi Luo Chun: A Taiwanese version of the famous Chinese green tea, made with this cultivar.

sensory.aroma: Elegant and ethereal Lilac, Gardenia, Cream, Fresh Mountain Air
sensory.flavor: Exceptionally smooth, buttery, and sweet with a profound and lasting aftertaste (huigan).
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Thick, soupy, and viscous with a very soft, creamy texture. The liquor is a pale, luminous golden-green.

qing-xin-da-mao.description: 'Green Heart Big Hairy'. The indispensable cultivar for creating Taiwan's famous Oriental Beauty oolong. This tea's unique honey and muscat grape flavor is not from the leaf itself, but from its reaction to the bites of a tiny insect, the tea leafhopper. The cultivar's specific chemistry is perfectly suited to this remarkable transformation.
qing-xin-da-mao.plantType: Sprawling, semi-upright bush, can be unruly (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
qing-xin-da-mao.environment: Thrives in the hot, humid, and lower-altitude (100-400m) environments of northwestern Taiwan where the tea leafhopper (Jacobiasca formosana) is abundant.
qing-xin-da-mao.processing: The entire process relies on nature; the tea must be bitten by the leafhopper. Processing then aims to highlight the resulting aromatic compounds. The leaves are handled gently to preserve their unique character.
qing-xin-da-mao.oxidation: Undergoes heavy oxidation (60-70%), which is crucial for developing the complex honey and ripe fruit flavors that are created in response to the insect bites.
qing-xin-da-mao.roasting: Completely unroasted. The rich, deep flavors are a result of oxidation, not heat. A finishing bake is used for drying only.
qing-xin-da-mao.versatility: Extremely specialized. This cultivar's identity and value are entirely dependent on the presence of the tea leafhopper and the specific processing of Oriental Beauty oolong.

Oriental Beauty Oolong (Dong Fang Mei Re.Bai Hao Oolong: Its sole, famous expression. A heavily oxidized, unroasted, multi-colored leaf oolong with a profound honey-fruit character derived from insect bites.

sensory.aroma: Intoxicating Muscat Grape, Ripe Peach, Wild Honey, Cinnamon
sensory.flavor: Sweet, complex, multi-layered fruit with a smooth, honeyed finish.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Full-bodied, smooth, and sweet with no bitterness. The liquor is a beautiful, bright reddish-orange.

qing-xin-gan-zhi.description: 'Green Heart Orange'. An older, traditional Taiwanese oolong cultivar that was more prominent before the widespread adoption of Qing Xin Oolong. It is known for producing a clean, fragrant, and slightly more vegetal Baozhong oolong and is a parent of the famous Si Ji Chun cultivar.
qing-xin-gan-zhi.plantType: Semi-upright bush, considered a more 'rustic' cultivar (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
qing-xin-gan-zhi.environment: Well-suited to the lower-altitude, humid basin environments like those found around Taipei.
qing-xin-gan-zhi.processing: Processing is straightforward, following the traditional twisted-leaf Baozhong style. The goal is to preserve a fresh, green character.
qing-xin-gan-zhi.oxidation: Undergoes very light oxidation (10-20%) to maintain its fresh, green, and floral notes.
qing-xin-gan-zhi.roasting: Unroasted, aside from a final drying bake. Its delicate character is not suited for roasting.
qing-xin-gan-zhi.versatility: Low versatility. It is a specialist for producing a classic, traditional style of Baozhong oolong.

Baozhong Oolong.Traditional Baozhong: Its classic expression. A twisted-leaf, lightly oxidized oolong with a very clean, fresh, and vegetal-floral profile.

sensory.aroma: Fresh green florals, cut grass, vegetal notes
sensory.flavor: Clean, brisk, and refreshing with a light sweetness.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Lighter-bodied and more brisk than Qing Xin Oolong, with a clean finish. The liquor is a clear, pale green-yellow.

que-she.description: 'Sparrow's Tongue'. A rare and highly sought-after Wuyi Rock Oolong named for its small, pointed leaves. It is celebrated for its exceptionally refined and elegant character, a high, sharp floral fragrance, and a very clean, mineral-driven taste. It is often processed with a lighter roast to preserve its delicate nature.
que-she.plantType: Small-leaf, slow-growing, semi-upright bush (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
que-she.environment: Grows in specific, protected microclimates within the Wuyi Mountains. It is less common due to its lower yield and more demanding growing conditions.
que-she.processing: Processing Que She requires great finesse. The goal is to highlight its delicate, high-pitched aroma. The leaves, while small, are robust enough for Yancha processing but shine when handled with a lighter touch.
que-she.oxidation: Undergoes a standard medium oxidation (30-50%) to develop a base of flavor that supports, rather than overwhelms, its high-note aromatics.
que-she.roasting: Roasting is typically lighter than for other top-tier Yancha. A careful, low-temperature bake is used to bring out the mineral notes and add smoothness while preserving the vibrant floral fragrance.
que-she.versatility: Highly specialized. Que She is an expression of a more elegant and aromatic style of Wuyi Rock Oolong.

Wuyi Rock Oolong (Yancha).Que She Yancha: A highly refined and aromatic rock oolong, often with a lighter roast to preserve its delicate and penetrating floral notes.

sensory.aroma: High, sharp, and lingering white flowers (gardenia, jasmine), very clean
sensory.flavor: Elegant, sweet, mineral-driven, and exceptionally clean with a vibrant finish.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Silky, medium-bodied, and bright with a very pure texture. The liquor is a luminous golden-amber.

rou-gui.description: 'Cassia/Cinnamon'. A top-tier Wuyi Rock Oolong prized for its pronounced spicy aroma. One of the most popular Yancha cultivars today.

saemidori.description: 'Clear Green'. A modern elite cultivar prized for its vibrant color and low bitterness. A hybrid of Yabukita and Asatsuyu.

samidori.description: A foundational and highly reliable cultivar from Uji, Kyoto. It is a versatile workhorse for the high-end shaded tea industry, particularly for Matcha. It is prized for its excellent, vibrant green color, good umami, and a smooth, well-balanced flavor that is ideal for creating both thick ('koicha') and thin ('usucha') Matcha.

shi-da-cha.description: 'Persimmon Big Tea'. A truly unique and visually stunning cultivar from Taiping county in Anhui. It is defined by its massive leaves, which can be much larger than a person's hand. It is used exclusively to make Tai Ping Hou Kui, a green tea where the leaves are painstakingly pressed by hand, resulting in a long, flat, and beautiful finished product.
shi-da-cha.plantType: Large, robust bush with very strong branches to support its massive leaves (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
shi-da-cha.environment: Grows in the misty, mountainous region of the former Taiping prefecture (now Huangshan district), where the specific microclimate allows these large leaves to grow tenderly.
shi-da-cha.processing: The processing is highly specialized and laborious. After kill-green, each individual leaf is placed between layers of cloth and hand-pressed with rollers to create its flat, uniform shape. This requires immense patience and skill.
shi-da-cha.oxidation: Zero oxidation. The massive leaves are quickly pan-fired to halt enzymatic activity and preserve their vibrant green color and fresh aroma.
shi-da-cha.roasting: A gentle baking process follows the hand-pressing to slowly and evenly dry the large, thick leaves without scorching them or creating a roasted flavor.
shi-da-cha.versatility: Completely specialized. This unique, giant-leaf cultivar exists only to be made into the singular and iconic Tai Ping Hou Kui.

china: Anhui Province (Huangshan City - former Taiping County area)

Green Tea.Tai Ping Hou Kui ('Peaceful Monkey Leade: Its only expression. A green tea where individual, massive leaves are pan-fired and then pressed flat between layers of cloth, creating a visually unique tea with a powerful orchid aroma.

sensory.aroma: Powerful and lingering Orchid fragrance, fresh, clean, and slightly vegetal
sensory.flavor: Mellow, sweet, and smooth with a deep, lasting floral sweetness and no bitterness.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Thick, soupy, and incredibly smooth with a very refreshing character. The liquor is a clear, bright green-yellow.

shizu-7132.description: A famous un-registered cultivar from Shizuoka, renowned for its intense and unmistakable aroma of 'sakura-mochi'—a sweet, cherry blossom and glutinous rice scent. It is a natural mutation of Yabukita and offers a very popular and distinct aromatic experience.
shizu-7132.plantType: Vigorous, mid-budding bush (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
shizu-7132.environment: Grows well in Shizuoka and is prized by farmers who specialize in aromatic teas.
shizu-7132.processing: Processing for 7132 is all about preserving its signature coumarin compound, which is responsible for the sakura aroma. This requires careful handling and specific steaming and drying parameters.
shizu-7132.oxidation: Zero oxidation. The leaves are steamed immediately after harvest.
shizu-7132.roasting: A careful final drying roast is applied to enhance and fix the sweet, sakura-like aroma without creating any burnt notes.
shizu-7132.versatility: Specialized for Sencha. Its entire value is based on its singular and highly sought-after cherry blossom aroma, so it is not used for other tea styles.

Sencha.Sakura Aroma Sencha: Its sole expression. A green tea processed to maximize its unique sweet cherry blossom and rice cake aroma.

sensory.aroma: Intense sweet cherry blossom (sakura), steamed rice, salty cherry leaf
sensory.flavor: Sweet, floral, with a unique cherry-like flavor and a smooth finish.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Smooth, medium-bodied, and very aromatic. The liquor is a bright green-yellow.

shui-jin-gui.description: 'Golden Water Turtle'. Another of the four 'Si Da Ming Cong', this cultivar is steeped in a legend of being washed away by a flood and thriving in its new home. It is celebrated for its vibrant and highly fragrant character, striking a beautiful balance between bright, effusive floral notes (like gardenia and osmanthus) and the classic, creamy mineral base of a top-tier rock oolong.
shui-jin-gui.plantType: Vigorous, productive bush with a semi-upright growth habit (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
shui-jin-gui.environment: Grows well in the core production areas of the Wuyi Mountains, where the soil and climate help it develop its signature balance of aroma and texture.
shui-jin-gui.processing: but not so much that it damages the delicate and valuable floral fragrance.,Highly specialized. Like its 'Si Da Ming Cong' siblings
shui-jin-gui.oxidation: Shui Jin Gui is a singular expression of Wuyi Rock Oolong
shui-jin-gui.roasting: valued for its unique and legendary aromatic profile.

shui-xian.description: 'Water Sprite' or 'Narcissus'. A foundational Fujian oolong cultivar, famous for its versatility and profound transformation with age and processing. Young or lightly roasted Shui Xian is floral and bright, while heavily roasted or aged 'Lao Cong' (Old Grove) versions reveal deep, complex notes of aged wood, moss, and a resonant sweetness.
shui-xian.plantType: Versatile arbor type that can be a bush or a small tree (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis). Known for its large leaves.
shui-xian.environment: Highly adaptable. Thrives in the rocky terroir of Wuyi but also grows well in the clay soils of Southern Fujian. Old groves are in protected, high-humidity environments.
shui-xian.processing: Its large, robust leaves are highly forgiving and can withstand significant processing, whether it be the bruising of oolong production or the heavy oxidation of black tea. They are particularly well-suited to absorbing the character of a charcoal roast.
shui-xian.oxidation: Oxidation is highly variable, from a medium 30% for more floral styles to a heavy 60-70% for darker, more robust Yancha expressions that are destined for aging or heavy roasting.
shui-xian.roasting: Extremely responsive to roasting. This is the key variable that defines its style. Light roasting preserves its delicate floral notes, while multiple, heavy roasts build immense depth, complexity, and a smooth, woody character.
shui-xian.versatility: Highly versatile. Shui Xian is a master of transformation, capable of producing a wide spectrum of oolong styles from light and floral to dark and brooding. It also makes a respectable black tea.

china: Guangdong Province (as a base for Dan Cong)

Wuyi Rock Oolong (Yancha).Shui Xian Yancha: Can be lightly roasted for a floral, narcissus-like profile, or heavily roasted for a deep, woody, and smooth character.
Wuyi Rock Oolong (Yancha).Lao Cong Shui Xian: The most prized expression, from trees over 60 years old, yielding a uniquely thick, mossy, and complex tea.

Black Tea.Fujian Black Tea: Its large leaves can be processed into a sweet, mellow black tea.

sensory.aroma: Narcissus flower, aged wood, moss, damp forest floor (roasted/aged)
sensory.flavor: Smooth, resonant, deep, with a lingering sweetness. Can be bright and floral or dark and woody.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Exceptionally full, smooth, and viscous, especially from old groves. The liquor ranges from golden yellow to deep reddish-brown.

si-ji-chun.description: 'Four Seasons Spring'. A famously prolific and aromatic cultivar, discovered as a natural cross in the 1980s. It's named for its ability to be harvested almost year-round, while still producing a tea with an explosive, forward, and highly accessible floral aroma, primarily of gardenia and jasmine.
si-ji-chun.plantType: Extremely vigorous, dense, and highly productive bush (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
si-ji-chun.environment: Thrives in lower-altitude, warmer, and more humid climates, which allows for its near-constant flushing and harvesting.
si-ji-chun.processing: Processing is fast and efficient, aimed at capturing the cultivar's potent upfront aroma. It is a workhorse cultivar that responds well to standard green oolong processing.
si-ji-chun.oxidation: Oxidation is kept very light (10-20%) to ensure the final product is dominated by the fresh, powerful gardenia and jasmine notes.
si-ji-chun.roasting: Unroasted. Its value lies in its fresh floral aroma, which would be destroyed by any significant roasting.
si-ji-chun.versatility: Low versatility. While incredibly productive, it is a specialist in producing one type of tea: a fragrant, accessible, and affordable light oolong. It lacks the structure for other styles.

taiwan: Nantou County (Mingjian is the largest area)

Oolong Tea (Aromatic Style).Si Ji Chun Oolong: Almost always made as a very lightly oxidized, unroasted oolong (often in the twisted Baozhong style) to maximize its powerful, fresh floral aroma. It's a popular daily-drinker tea.

sensory.aroma: Intense, forward Gardenia, Jasmine, and other white flowers
sensory.flavor: Crisp, highly floral, and slightly pungent with a brisk finish.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Light-to-medium-bodied with a fresh, clean texture. The liquor is a pale green-yellow.

sofu.description: 'Blue Wind'. A modern aromatic cultivar, similar to Koshun, that is prized for its striking and unique fragrance. It produces a Sencha or light oolong with a powerful perfume-like aroma of black currant, citrus, and mint, representing a new wave of aromatic Japanese teas.
sofu.plantType: Vigorous, upright bush (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
sofu.environment: Adaptable to various climates, it is a key cultivar for the Saitama region.
sofu.processing: Like other aromatic cultivars, Sofu is processed with a gentle hand to preserve its volatile compounds. Light steaming is preferred to avoid damaging the unique aroma.
sofu.oxidation: Zero oxidation for the Sencha style. Steamed immediately after harvest.
sofu.roasting: A very light final drying roast is applied to stabilize the tea without diminishing its powerful, unique fragrance.
sofu.versatility: Moderately versatile. It is primarily used for creating unique aromatic Senchas and is also an excellent choice for making Japanese-style light oolongs.

Sencha.Aromatic Sencha: Used to create a Sencha with a very unique, zesty, and minty aromatic profile.

Japanese Oolong.Light Oolong: Its strong aromatics are well-suited for producing fragrant, lightly oxidized oolongs.

sensory.aroma: Striking black currant, citrus peel, mint
sensory.flavor: Bright, zesty, and aromatic with a refreshing, cool finish.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Smooth, light-to-medium-bodied, and very refreshing. The liquor is a pale green-yellow.

song-zhong.description: 'Song Dynasty Cultivar'. The apex predator of Phoenix Dan Cong oolongs, Song Zhong refers to teas made from the direct descendants of the oldest known tea tree on Wudong Mountain (reputed to be over 600 years old). It is an incredibly powerful, deep, and complex tea, known for its profound 'cha qi' (tea energy) and a layered flavor profile that can only be achieved through great age and perfect terroir.
song-zhong.plantType: Old, gnarled, and often moss-covered arbor trees with highly variable leaf shapes (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
song-zhong.environment: Grows exclusively on Wudong Mountain, the highest peak in the Phoenix range, in mineral-rich, yellowish-brown soil at very high altitudes (>1100m).
song-zhong.processing: Processing tea from such old trees is an immense responsibility. The tea master must use all their skill to translate the raw potential of the leaves into a finished tea that is worthy of its lineage. The process is slow, careful, and traditional.
song-zhong.oxidation: Undergoes a deep and complex oxidation process (can be 40-60% or more) that is carefully monitored to develop its multi-layered aromatic profile.
song-zhong.roasting: The roasting is deep, slow, and done in multiple stages over charcoal. This complex roasting process is essential for integrating the tea's powerful flavors, smoothing its texture, and creating a tea that will continue to age and improve for years.
song-zhong.versatility: The ultimate specialist. Song Zhong represents the highest achievement of the Dan Cong oolong style and is never made in any other way.

china: Guangdong Province (Chaozhou - only from Wudong Mountain)

Dan Cong Oolong (Grand Cru).Song Zhong Dan Cong: The pinnacle of Dan Cong. A deeply oxidized and carefully roasted tea that expresses immense complexity, depth, and power. It is not about a single fragrance, but a symphony of aromas.

sensory.aroma: Deep and complex; layers of tropical fruit, honey, wild flowers, incense, and wet stone
sensory.flavor: Profoundly complex, with a powerful mineral backbone, incredible sweetness, and an endless, evolving finish.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Extremely thick, viscous, and soupy with a powerful warming and energetic sensation ('cha qi'). The liquor is a deep, radiant orange-amber.

taiwanese-wild-tea.description: The native, indigenous tea species of Taiwan, genetically distinct from the more common Camellia sinensis. It grows wild in the central mountain range. While not a major commercial crop, it is wild-harvested for specialty teas and is crucially important as genetic stock for breeding, most famously as a parent of the Hong Yu #18 'Ruby' cultivar.
taiwanese-wild-tea.plantType: Wild-growing tree that can become very large and old (Camellia formosensis).
taiwanese-wild-tea.environment: Grows wild in the protected, biodiverse forests of Taiwan's central mountain range at various altitudes.
taiwanese-wild-tea.processing: Processing is often experimental and done by boutique producers. The wild-harvested leaves are precious and are typically handled with care to express their unique, wild character.
taiwanese-wild-tea.oxidation: Typically undergoes full oxidation to be made into black tea, which seems to best complement its wild, woody, and herbaceous notes.
taiwanese-wild-tea.roasting: No roasting. The tea is dried with hot air.
taiwanese-wild-tea.versatility: Not a commercial production cultivar, but a specialty item and a vital genetic resource. It is a wild plant, not a cultivated one in the traditional sense.

Specialty Tea.Wild Black Tea: When processed as a black tea, it has a unique, wild, and herbaceous character.
Specialty Tea.Scented Tea: Its unique leaves are sometimes used as a base for scented or blended teas.

Breeding.Genetic Stock: Its most important role, providing unique genes for creating modern hybrids like Hong Yu #18.

sensory.aroma: Wild, herbaceous, forest floor, mushroom, sweet wood
sensory.flavor: Unique and complex, with notes of sweet wood, herbs, and a deep, wild sweetness.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Surprisingly smooth and clean with a deep, lingering aftertaste. The liquor can be reddish-brown or dark amber.

takachiho.description: A classic cultivar specific to the regions in Kyushu that specialize in 'Kamairicha' or pan-fired green tea. It is prized for its ability to withstand the high heat of pan-firing, producing a green tea with a beautiful nutty and roasted aroma ('kama-ka') that is very different from the vegetal notes of steamed Sencha.
takachiho.plantType: Medium-sized, robust bush adapted to pan-firing (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
takachiho.environment: Thrives in the warm climate of southern Kyushu, particularly Miyazaki, the heart of Kamairicha production.
takachiho.processing: the leaves are fired in a hot iron pan or rotating drum
takachiho.oxidation: a technique originally from China. This high
takachiho.roasting: dry heat creates the characteristic nutty aroma.,Zero oxidation. The pan-firing immediately halts all enzymatic activity.,No roasting in the traditional sense. The pan-firing process itself serves to dry the tea and create its signature roasted flavor profile.,Extremely specialized. Takachiho is a cornerstone cultivar for the unique
takachiho.versatility:
non-steamed Kamairicha style of Japanese green tea.
Benifuki,べにふうき,'Red Riches'. Japan's most famous and important black tea cultivar. It is a powerful hybrid of Assamica varieties

Kamairicha (Pan-Fired Green Tea).Classic Kamairicha: Its premier expression. A pan-fired green tea with a signature nutty, roasted corn aroma and a refreshing, non-astringent flavor.

tie-guan-yin.description: 'Iron Goddess of Mercy'. A legendary oolong from Anxi, China, celebrated for its complex floral aroma and lingering sweet aftertaste, known as 'Guan Yin Yun'. Its robust leaves can withstand intricate processing, yielding two distinct styles: a modern, vibrantly floral green style and a traditional, deeply roasted style with notes of fruit and caramel.
tie-guan-yin.plantType: Semi-upright arbor type with strong, reddish branches (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis). Known for its resilience.
tie-guan-yin.environment: Prefers the acidic, iron-rich red soil and misty, humid climate of Anxi's mid-level mountains (300-1,000m).
tie-guan-yin.processing: The cultivar's thick, durable leaves are its greatest asset, able to withstand the repeated bruising, shaking, and rolling required to develop its complex aromatics without breaking. This makes it ideal for both light and heavy processing.
tie-guan-yin.oxidation: For the modern green style, oxidation is kept low (15-25%). For the traditional baked style, oxidation is higher (30-50%), which develops a fruity base that can stand up to the heavy roasting.
tie-guan-yin.roasting: The green style is unroasted or given a very light drying bake. The traditional style is defined by its 'hong bei' (烘焙) charcoal roasting, which can take place over many hours at low temperatures to build deep, complex flavors.
tie-guan-yin.versatility: Highly versatile within the oolong category. Its two primary styles are worlds apart. It can also be processed into a unique, floral black tea, though this is less common.

Modern Green Style Oolong.Anxi Tie Guan Yin: Lightly oxidized and unroasted, emphasizing a vibrant, creamy, and intensely floral character like fresh lilac and orchid.

Traditional Baked Style Oolong.Anxi Tie Guan Yin (Nong Xiang): Medium oxidized and subjected to multiple, slow charcoal roasts, creating deep notes of roasted nuts, apricot, and a warming mineral finish.

Taiwanese Style Oolong.Muzha Tie Guan Yin: A heavily oxidized and roasted style with a distinct ripe fruit acidity and robust character.

sensory.aroma: Intense Orchid, Lilac, Osmanthus, Toasted Grains (if roasted)
sensory.flavor: Creamy, Buttery, sweet vegetal notes (green style), or Ripe Apricot, Caramel, Mineral (baked style)
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Thick, smooth, and full-bodied with a signature long, sweet, and cooling finish (Guan Yin Yun). Liquor is pale jade to golden amber.

tie-luo-han.description: 'Iron Arhat'. One of the four original 'Si Da Ming Cong' (Great Famous Bushes) of the Wuyi Mountains. Tie Luo Han is a powerful and assertive tea, steeped in history and known for its strong 'cha qi' (tea energy), warming character, and complex flavor profile with distinct medicinal and spicy undertones.
tie-luo-han.plantType: Sturdy, semi-upright bush with strong branches, well-suited to its rocky environment (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
tie-luo-han.environment: Grows in the core 'Zhengyan' region of the Wuyi Mountains, where the unique mineral composition of the soil contributes to its powerful character.
tie-luo-han.processing: The processing of Tie Luo Han aims to tame its natural intensity while enhancing its complexity. Its robust leaves can handle the high heat and repeated steps necessary to develop its deep, warming character.
tie-luo-han.oxidation: Undergoes heavy oxidation (50-70%) to build a rich, complex base that can support its inherent strength and the intensity of the roast. This step is crucial for developing its fruity and herbal notes.
tie-luo-han.roasting: Requires a strong, masterful charcoal roast. The goal is to bake the flavor deep into the leaf, smoothing out any rough edges while amplifying its warming, spicy, and mineral-driven qualities.
tie-luo-han.versatility: Completely specialized. Tie Luo Han is a singular expression of Yancha. Its identity is inseparable from the traditional, heavily processed rock oolong style.

Wuyi Rock Oolong (Yancha).Tie Luo Han Yancha: This is its sole expression. It is a heavily oxidized and roasted oolong designed to be bold and complex, showcasing its unique herbal and mineral profile.

sensory.aroma: Medicinal herbs, ginger spice, dark honey, hot metal, charcoal
sensory.flavor: Strong, warming, with a distinct mineralic and metallic finish. Notes of dark fruit and burnt sugar.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Thick, viscous, and warming with a powerful, long-lasting aftertaste and noticeable 'cha qi'. The liquor is a deep, dark amber.

tong-tian-xiang.description: 'Heavenly Aroma' or 'Heaven-Reaching Aroma'. An old and highly revered Dan Cong cultivar from Wudong Mountain, the highest peak of the Phoenix range. It is known for its exceptionally powerful, penetrating, and complex aroma, often with notes of ginger and exotic spices, and a very strong 'cha qi' (tea energy).
tong-tian-xiang.plantType: Old Dan Cong arbor, often with a tall, upright growth habit (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
tong-tian-xiang.environment: Grows exclusively on the high slopes of Wudong Mountain, where the unique terroir is responsible for its incredible power and aromatic complexity.
tong-tian-xiang.processing: from spicy to fruity to floral.,Receives a masterful charcoal roast. The roast must be precise and deep enough to integrate the tea's powerful flavors and create a smooth texture
tong-tian-xiang.oxidation: without damaging the prized aromatic compounds.,The ultimate specialist. Tong Tian Xiang is a rare
tong-tian-xiang.roasting:
high-end Dan Cong oolong that represents the pinnacle of the style.
Long Jing #43,龙井43号,The most widespread and commercially important modern cultivar for West Lake Long Jing tea. Developed in the 1970s
tong-tian-xiang.versatility: it is prized by farmers for its early budding (allowing for a prized pre-Qingming harvest)

Dan Cong Oolong.Tong Tian Xiang Dan Cong: A 'grand cru' Dan Cong oolong, processed with masterful skill to showcase its potent and multi-layered aromatic profile.

ujihikari.description: 'Light of Uji'. A premier modern cultivar from Uji, Kyoto, developed specifically for shaded tea production. It is known for its elegant, refined character, a brilliant green color, and a sweet, clean umami profile that is slightly less brothy and more refined than Goko. It is a top choice for competition-grade Gyokuro and Matcha.

wu-yi.description: 'Wuyi'. This refers to tea plants that were originally brought to Taiwan from the Wuyi Mountains in Fujian, likely a Shui Xian type. In Taiwan, this cultivar is used to create a medium-oxidized and medium-roast oolong that pays homage to its Yancha roots. It produces a tea with a characteristic balance of woody, fruity, and mineral notes.
wu-yi.plantType: Sturdy, semi-arbor bush (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
wu-yi.environment: Grows well in the mid-elevation regions of central Taiwan, such as Lugu in Nantou County.
wu-yi.processing: Processing follows the traditional Dong Ding method. The leaves are moderately bruised and oxidized to develop a solid flavor base, and then skillfully roasted to add depth and complexity.
wu-yi.oxidation: Undergoes medium oxidation (30-40%) to create a balance between retaining some floral notes and developing a fruity, substantive character that is ideal for roasting.
wu-yi.roasting: Perfectly suited for a medium charcoal roast. The roasting enhances its nutty and woody notes, creates a caramel-like sweetness, and gives the tea a comforting, smooth character.
wu-yi.versatility: Specialized for the traditional roasted oolong style. It is a key cultivar in the history of Dong Ding oolong and is not used for light, green styles.

Traditional Oolong.Taiwanese Wuyi Oolong: A medium-oxidized and medium-roast oolong, often made in the style of traditional Dong Ding. It bridges the gap between fragrant high mountain oolongs and heavily roasted teas.

sensory.aroma: Woody, floral, with notes of roasted nuts and dried fruit
sensory.flavor: A balanced profile of fruit, wood, and a subtle minerality with a pleasant roasted sweetness.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Medium-to-full-bodied, smooth, and satisfying with a warming finish. The liquor is a classic amber color.

wuyi-cai-cha.description: 'Wuyi Vegetable Tea'. This is not a single clonal cultivar, but the original, genetically diverse heirloom 'population' of small-leaf tea bushes native to the Wuyi region. It is the authentic, historical cultivar used to create the world's first black tea, Lapsang Souchong. Unsmoked, it produces a black tea of incredible elegance and sweetness.
wuyi-cai-cha.plantType: Variable, typically small, hardy bushes that have adapted over centuries (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
wuyi-cai-cha.environment: Grows wild and cultivated in the high-altitude, protected ecosystem of the Tongmu Nature Preserve within the Wuyi Mountains, the birthplace of black tea.
wuyi-cai-cha.processing: For unsmoked Lapsang, the processing is a classic black tea method (withering, rolling, full oxidation, drying). For the smoked version, the key final step is drying the tea on racks above smoldering, resinous pine wood fires.
wuyi-cai-cha.oxidation: Undergoes full oxidation (100%) to be classified as a black tea. The small leaves oxidize relatively quickly, creating a refined rather than a robustly malty flavor.
wuyi-cai-cha.roasting: The unsmoked version is dried with clean, hot air. The smoked version's 'roast' is a low-temperature smoke-drying process that infuses the leaves with a powerful pine aroma.
wuyi-cai-cha.versatility: Highly specialized for black tea. Its entire history and identity are tied to being the original Lapsang Souchong cultivar, whether smoked or unsmoked.

china: Fujian Province (Wuyi Mountains, specifically Tongmu Village)

Black Tea.Unsmoked Lapsang Souchong (Zheng Shan Xi: Its highest expression. An elegant, smooth black tea with natural notes of longan fruit and sweet potato.
Black Tea.Smoked Lapsang Souchong: The famous export version, which is dried over pine wood fires, imparting a strong, smoky, campfire aroma.

sensory.aroma: Longan fruit, sweet potato, honey (unsmoked); or Pine smoke, campfire, leather (smoked)
sensory.flavor: Naturally sweet, clean, and elegant with a smooth, fruity character (unsmoked).
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Silky, smooth, and medium-bodied with a very clean and sweet aftertaste. The liquor is a bright, clear reddish-orange.

xing-ren-xiang.description: 'Almond Fragrance'. A classic and distinct Phoenix Dan Cong oolong fragrance type. It is prized for its clear, focused, and unmistakable aroma and flavor of bitter almond, marzipan, and apricot kernel. It offers a unique, nutty departure from the more common floral or fruity Dan Cong profiles.
xing-ren-xiang.plantType: Medium-sized arbor with ovate, dark green leaves (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
xing-ren-xiang.environment: Grows in the high-altitude, mineral-rich soils of the Phoenix Mountains, which provide the base texture and sweetness for its nutty profile to emerge.
xing-ren-xiang.processing: The key to producing Xing Ren Xiang is identifying the specific trees that carry this genetic trait and then processing them in a way that highlights it. The bruising and oxidation must be managed to favor the development of these specific nutty aromatic compounds.
xing-ren-xiang.oxidation: Undergoes a standard medium oxidation (30-45%) for Dan Cong, which provides the necessary foundation for its unique flavor profile to develop fully.
xing-ren-xiang.roasting: The roast for Xing Ren Xiang is often a bit heavier than for very floral Dan Congs. A medium roast helps to enhance the nutty, toasted character and integrate it with the tea's natural sweetness and minerality.
xing-ren-xiang.versatility: Highly specialized. This is a classic, specific fragrance profile within the Dan Cong oolong family and is not made in any other style.

Dan Cong Oolong.Xing Ren Xiang Dan Cong: A medium-oxidized and roasted Dan Cong where the processing is carefully controlled to bring out the specific almond-like aromatic compounds.

sensory.aroma: Clear and focused Bitter Almond, Marzipan, Apricot Kernel
sensory.flavor: Nutty, sweet, with a distinct almond-like character and a clean, pleasant bitterness in the finish.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Smooth, medium-to-full-bodied with a unique, slightly astringent finish that enhances its nutty character. The liquor is a bright golden-amber.

ya-shi-xiang.description: 'Duck Shit Fragrance'. A Phoenix Dan Cong oolong with a famously off-putting name that conceals a sublimely beautiful tea. It is celebrated for its uniquely creamy mouthfeel and an intense, intoxicating floral aroma of gardenia and honeysuckle, which is completely at odds with its rustic name.
ya-shi-xiang.plantType: Upright, vigorous arbor with dark, slightly larger leaves (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
ya-shi-xiang.environment: Grows in the high-altitude terroir of the Phoenix Mountains. Its unique creamy character is said to come from the specific soil of its home village.
ya-shi-xiang.processing: The processing of Ya Shi Xiang is meticulous, with a strong focus on the withering and bruising stages to develop not only the high floral notes but also the compounds that contribute to its exceptionally creamy mouthfeel.
ya-shi-xiang.oxidation: Oxidation is typically in the medium range (30-45%). This level is crucial for transforming the leaf's potential into the rich, complex, and layered floral-creamy profile it is famous for.
ya-shi-xiang.roasting: Usually receives a light charcoal roast. The goal is to dry the tea thoroughly and enhance its creamy texture and sweetness without diminishing the high-pitched gardenia and honeysuckle aromatics.
ya-shi-xiang.versatility: Completely specialized for the Dan Cong oolong style. Its legendary status is entirely built on its unique aroma and texture when processed in this traditional manner.

Dan Cong Oolong.Ya Shi Xiang Dan Cong: Its only expression is a medium-oxidized and lightly roasted oolong, with processing focused on developing its signature creamy texture alongside its intense floral aroma.

sensory.aroma: Intense Gardenia, Honeysuckle, Jasmine, Cream, Almond Milk
sensory.flavor: Richly floral, sweet, with a distinct creamy or milky undertone that softens the entire profile.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Uniquely thick, creamy, and velvety smooth. Coats the mouth with a long, sweet, floral aftertaste. The liquor is a rich golden color.

yabukita.description: 'North of the Bamboo Grove'. The undisputed king of Japanese tea, accounting for over 75% of all tea production in Japan. Discovered in 1908, it became the national standard due to its hardiness, high yield, and a perfectly balanced flavor profile of umami and refreshing astringency. It is the benchmark against which all other Japanese green teas are measured.
yabukita.plantType: Hardy, vigorous, and highly adaptable mid-budding bush (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
yabukita.environment: Extremely adaptable to a wide range of climates and altitudes, from the cool mountains of Shizuoka to the warm plains of Kagoshima.
yabukita.processing: from light steaming (Asamushi) to deep steaming (Fukamushi).,Zero oxidation. The leaves are steamed immediately after harvest to halt all enzymatic activity. The steaming time (30-120 seconds) determines the style (Asamushi
yabukita.roasting: or Fukamushi).,Receives a final drying roast ('hi-ire') to stabilize the tea and enhance its aroma. This is typically a light bake
yabukita.versatility: not a heavy roast.,Extremely versatile. It is the workhorse of the Japanese tea industry and can be skillfully crafted into almost any type of Japanese tea

Sencha.Classic Sencha: Its most iconic expression. A perfectly balanced steamed green tea with classic umami and vegetal notes.

Fukamushi Sencha.Deep-Steamed Sencha: Its flavor holds up well to deep-steaming, creating a bolder, greener, and less astringent tea.

Gyokuro & Matcha.Shaded Teas: While not an elite shading cultivar, it is widely used to produce reliable and good quality Gyokuro and Matcha.

ying-xiang.description: 'Welcome Fragrance'. A new-generation oolong cultivar released by TRES in 2014, Ying Xiang was bred to have the elegant floral character of Qing Xin but with more intensity and a tropical twist. It is known for its clear, sophisticated, floral aroma reminiscent of osmanthus and lily.
ying-xiang.plantType: Vigorous, upright bush with good productivity.
ying-xiang.environment: Adaptable to a range of mid-altitude environments, performing well in the established oolong regions of Nantou.
ying-xiang.processing: Processing is focused on highlighting its refined floral notes. It requires gentle handling during withering and bruising to develop its complex bouquet without introducing any undesirable green notes.
ying-xiang.oxidation: Undergoes light oxidation (15-25%), which is ideal for showcasing its high-note floral aromatics.
ying-xiang.roasting: Unroasted. Like other highly aromatic Taiwanese oolongs, any significant roasting would damage its primary characteristic.
ying-xiang.versatility: Specialized for light, aromatic oolongs. It was designed to be a modern, high-fragrance alternative to Qing Xin and excels in that role.

Oolong Tea (Aromatic Style).Ying Xiang Oolong: Best expressed as a lightly oxidized, unroasted oolong, often in the twisted Baozhong style, to maximize its elegant and intense floral character.

sensory.aroma: Elegant tropical flowers, Osmanthus, Lily, fresh sweetness
sensory.flavor: Clean, intensely floral, and sweet with a very smooth and refined profile.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Smooth, silky, and medium-bodied with a long, purely aromatic finish. The liquor is a clear, pale gold.

yiwu-da-ye-zhong.description: 'Yiwu Big Leaf Variety'. A famous sub-variety of the Da Ye (Assamica) varietal from the historic Yiwu mountains, one of the original Six Great Tea Mountains. In contrast to the power of Mengku, Yiwu teas are prized for their exceptional softness, elegance, and 'rou' (柔) character. They are known for having very low bitterness, a thick, soupy texture, and a prominent floral fragrance.
yiwu-da-ye-zhong.plantType: Large arbor trees, often with a more sprawling growth habit and very large leaves (Camellia sinensis var. assamica).
yiwu-da-ye-zhong.environment: Grows in the protected, high-humidity, and biodiverse forests of the Yiwu mountain range, which contributes to its elegant and gentle nature.
yiwu-da-ye-zhong.processing: Processing follows the traditional Sheng Pu'er method (pan-fire, roll, sun-dry). The skill lies in preserving the tea's inherent softness and aromatic delicacy throughout the process.
yiwu-da-ye-zhong.oxidation: Minimal oxidation (<5%) from processing. The focus is on preserving the gentle, floral nature of the fresh leaves for aging.
yiwu-da-ye-zhong.roasting: No roasting. Sun-drying is the essential final step that defines Pu'er and allows the tea to age gracefully over decades.
yiwu-da-ye-zhong.versatility: Extremely specialized. Yiwu Da Ye is a prized 'terroir-specific' cultivar used exclusively for making soft, elegant, and highly sought-after Sheng Pu'er.

china: Yunnan Province (Xishuangbanna Prefecture, specifically Yiwu Township)

Sheng (Raw) Pu'er.Yiwu Pu'er: Its only expression. An elegant, soft, and highly aromatic raw Pu'er celebrated for its smooth texture and incredible aging potential into a very refined tea.

sensory.aroma: Elegant, high-pitched floral notes (wild orchid), honey, rock sugar
sensory.flavor: Very soft, gentle, and sweet with minimal bitterness and a long, cooling, sweet aftertaste.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Exceptionally thick, smooth, and soupy ('tang gan'). Coats the mouth and throat. The liquor is a clear, bright golden-yellow.

yutakamidori.description: 'Abundant Green'. An early-budding cultivar, very popular in the warmer Kagoshima region, especially for deep-steamed Sencha.

zairai.description: 'Conventional' or 'Native'. This is not a single cultivar, but the crucial designation for Japan's heirloom, seed-propagated tea populations. Before modern clonal agriculture, all tea was Zairai. Each Zairai field is a unique, genetically diverse ecosystem, producing a tea with a complex, rustic, and deeply terroir-driven flavor that cannot be replicated by a single clone.
zairai.plantType: Highly variable; a genetically diverse population of bushes and trees that have adapted to their specific location over centuries (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
zairai.environment: Extremely well-adapted to its specific, long-standing local environment. Zairai fields are often found in older, more remote, or organically-focused tea gardens.
zairai.processing: Processing Zairai requires great skill from the tea master, as the leaves are not uniform in size, shape, or moisture content. The master must adapt their technique to the specific characteristics of each unique batch.
zairai.oxidation: Oxidation can vary completely depending on the tea being made, from zero (for Sencha) to full (for Wakocha).
zairai.roasting: Roasting is highly dependent on the final tea style. Zairai can be unroasted for Sencha, or heavily roasted to produce a deep, comforting Hojicha.
zairai.versatility: The ultimate in versatility. As a genetically diverse population, Zairai can be crafted into almost any style of tea. Each expression is a unique snapshot of a specific place and time, prized by connoisseurs for its depth and authenticity.

Sencha.Zairai Sencha: A complex, often mineralic green tea with deep character.

Bancha.Zairai Bancha: Often used for rustic, everyday Bancha or Hojicha.

Wakocha.Zairai Black Tea: Can be oxidized into a unique, non-malty black tea.

sensory.aroma: Wild herbs, woody, mineralic, varies greatly by region
sensory.flavor: Complex, deep, gentle sweetness, often with a pleasant, mild astringency that reflects its wild nature.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Varies greatly, but often has a clean, deep, and lingering character. Liquor color depends entirely on processing.

zhenghe-da-bai.description: 'Zhenghe Big White'. A close cousin to Fuding Da Bai, this cultivar is the foundation of white tea from the inland Zhenghe region. It is known for producing white teas that are fuller-bodied, darker in color, and deeper in flavor compared to those from Fuding, often with notes of dried fruit and wood. It is also a key cultivar for some Fujian black teas.
zhenghe-da-bai.plantType: Vigorous, semi-arbor type with a later budding time than Fuding Da Bai (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
zhenghe-da-bai.environment: Thrives in the cooler, high-altitude, and foggy inland environment of Zhenghe County. The longer growing cycle contributes to its deeper flavor accumulation.
zhenghe-da-bai.processing: The processing for Zhenghe white tea is similar to Fuding (long withering, gentle drying), but the later-budding, slower-growing nature of the cultivar results in a different final product. The leaves accumulate different compounds, leading to a deeper flavor.
zhenghe-da-bai.oxidation: Undergoes a slightly higher degree of natural oxidation during its longer withering process compared to Fuding teas, which contributes to its darker color and deeper flavor profile.
zhenghe-da-bai.roasting: Like other white teas, it is not roasted. The final step is a thorough, low-temperature drying.
zhenghe-da-bai.versatility: Quite versatile. It is a star performer for a distinct style of white tea and is also one of the classic, foundational cultivars for traditional Fujian black tea (Congou/Gongfu style).

china: Fujian Province (Zhenghe County and surrounding inland areas)

White Tea.Zhenghe Silver Needle & White Peony: These teas are known for being deeper, often with notes of dark fruit, hay, and a fuller, rounder mouthfeel than their Fuding counterparts.

Black Tea.Panyong Congou: This cultivar is traditionally used to make this classic Fujian black tea, known for its smooth, sweet profile.

sensory.aroma: Dried date, autumn leaves, subtle woodiness, hay
sensory.flavor: Deeper natural sweetness, hints of dark fruit (fig, date), and a slightly earthy undertone.

zhi-lan-xiang.description: 'Orchid Fragrance'. A benchmark Phoenix Dan Cong oolong, considered one of the most classic and elegant expressions of a floral Dan Cong. It is prized for its refined, high-pitched, and pure orchid fragrance, which is less fruity than Mi Lan Xiang and more focused and delicate, representing a connoisseur's floral profile.
zhi-lan-xiang.plantType: Medium-sized arbor with long, yellowish-green leaves (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
zhi-lan-xiang.environment: Grows in the high-altitude terroir of Wudong Mountain within the Phoenix range, which is considered the best area for producing Dan Congs with elegance and complexity.
zhi-lan-xiang.processing: The processing of Zhi Lan Xiang requires an expert hand. The goal is to achieve a perfect, clean expression of its orchid aroma without any off-notes. This demands precise control over withering, bruising, and oxidation.
zhi-lan-xiang.oxidation: Oxidation is typically in the lighter-medium range (25-35%). This keeps the profile bright, fresh, and focused on the high-note floral aromatics.
zhi-lan-xiang.roasting: Receives a very light, low-temperature finishing roast. The bake is just enough to ensure stability and remove any residual greenness, allowing the pure orchid fragrance to be the star.
zhi-lan-xiang.versatility: Completely specialized for the high-end Dan Cong oolong style. Its value is derived entirely from its masterful expression of a pure and elegant floral profile.

china: Guangdong Province (Chaozhou - Phoenix Mountains, especially Wudong)

Dan Cong Oolong.Zhi Lan Xiang Dan Cong: A masterfully processed Dan Cong oolong where every step is aimed at capturing the pure, elegant, and ethereal orchid aroma.

sensory.aroma: Refined, high-pitched Orchid, Iris, fresh greenery
sensory.flavor: Elegant, sweet, and intensely floral with a clean mineral backbone and a very long, fragrant aftertaste.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Silky, smooth, and vibrant with a characteristic cooling sensation in the throat. The liquor is a very clear, pale gold.

zi-juan.description: 'Purple Juan'. A unique and modern Yunnan cultivar developed from a natural purple-leaf mutation of the Da Ye (Assamica) varietal. Its most striking feature is its deep purple leaves, buds, and stems, a result of a very high concentration of anthocyanins. The finished tea has a distinct flavor profile, often with berry-like and slightly medicinal notes.
zi-juan.plantType: Upright, medium-sized bush with a striking purple coloration throughout the plant (Camellia sinensis var. assamica).
zi-juan.environment: Grown in the high-altitude tea regions of Yunnan, where strong sunlight is thought to enhance its purple pigmentation.
zi-juan.processing: Processing Zi Juan requires care to manage its higher-than-average astringency and bitterness. The processing method (green, black, or Pu'er) dramatically changes its final flavor profile.
zi-juan.oxidation: Oxidation levels can vary from none (green/Pu'er) to full (black tea). Full oxidation can help to mellow some of its natural astringency.
zi-juan.roasting: No roasting is typically applied. Like Pu'er, it is often sun-dried for green tea styles, or oven-dried for black tea styles.
zi-juan.versatility: Moderately versatile. It can be crafted into several different types of tea, but its unique and assertive flavor profile means it will always be a niche, specialty product rather than a mainstream tea.

china: Yunnan Province (various regions, often as a specialty crop)

Green Tea.Purple Needle: A sun-dried green tea (similar to Sheng Pu'er processing) that highlights its unique briskness and color.

Black Tea.Purple Black: A fully oxidized tea that has a unique reddish-purple liquor and a fruity, slightly astringent flavor.

Pu'er Tea.Purple Pu'er: Can be pressed into cakes like traditional Sheng Pu'er, valued for its unique character and appearance.
